source:
Father,

As I was preparing for my journey last night, I attempted to find a certain lute of mine which was the favorite among my collection. It has gone missing from its case. I'm certain Hamlet stole it. If you could somehow arrange its return during my absence, I would be overjoyed. Please don't hesitate to get Bernardo involved.

source: Elise's Final Words
target: 伊莉丝的临终之言

source:
I am Elise, lady to the Queen, servant all my life. They say I am mad with fever. But this is truth. Hear my final story, if you are able, if you care a whit, if you can know its significance.

I was barely more than a child myself when Simona was first let into the castle, a glowing vision of a girl dressed in a peasant's rags. Even then the head scullery maid ordered her hair be covered so she didn't attract 'attention'. In the end, it made no difference.

Simona was kind to me. This, I recall. I often helped the girl with her work as she braided the Queen's hair. After she was finished, Queen Astrid would beg her to stay, to tell stories. Simona had a way with stories. She never refused. And when King Alexander came to bed and woo Simona, who was she to refuse him, either?

Then there was the book. That horrid book... Simona brought it home. From where? Who gave it to her? I still don't know. Four days later, news of Queen Astrid's sudden death shocked the castle into mute horror, and Simona was quietly whisked away to the King's chambers. She was now the King's only lover. A low-born nobody with the power to rule nations.

The guards whispered of Queen Astrid's body: of how she died with her own nails lodged in her throat, the flesh torn, gone abruptly and thoroughly mad, her blood seeping through the keep tower's floor.

Simona came to me early one morning when it was still dark, inconsolably upset and without a light. "The book is cursed," She whispered to me in the darkness, her face wet with tears. "Elise, you don't understand. I was trapped in Elsinore for ever, for a thousand years or more. I saw every outcome I could, every possible version of this world, and it was all rotten. What could I do, Elise? What could I do? The book made me choose, and I chose to let Astrid rot with it all, so I could rule..."

She kissed me goodbye and pressed a coin into my hand. "I cannot hide from God," she said. "But I cannot stay in Elsinore. Tell no one where I went. Promise me, Elise."

And here I am, breaking that promise. I know Simona lives. What happened that insane week all those years ago? What will become of little Ophelia and Laertes, and my beloved husband I left behind? I will go to my grave not knowing.

Should my family ever read this, know this: I lived a far luckier life than any woman of my station ought to have enjoyed. But the luckiest thing in my world was always you.
target:
我是伊莉丝，王后的侍女，一辈子都在服侍人。他们说我发烧烧疯了。但这些都是真的。请听听我最后的故事，只要你还能听，只要你还有一点在乎，只要你能明白它意味着什么。

西蒙娜初次获准进入城堡时，我自己也才刚过孩童的年纪。她穿着农家人的破衣烂衫，却美得光彩照人。那时，洗碗女仆的领班就命令她把头发遮起来，免得引来“注意”。到头来，这也没起什么作用。

西蒙娜待我很好。这一点，我记得。她为王后编头发时，我常常帮她做事。编完之后，阿斯特丽德王后总会央求她留下来讲故事。西蒙娜很会讲故事。她从不拒绝。而当亚历山大国王来向西蒙娜求欢、与她同床时，她又哪有资格拒绝他呢？

后来，那本书出现了。那本可怕的书……西蒙娜把它带回了家。从哪里来的？是谁给她的？我至今都不知道。四天后，阿斯特丽德王后猝死的消息让整个城堡陷入惊恐，鸦雀无声，而西蒙娜被悄悄带进了国王的寝宫。如今，她成了国王唯一的情人。一个出身卑微的无名之辈，却有了统治列国的权力。

卫兵们悄声议论着阿斯特丽德王后的尸体：她死时，自己的指甲还扎在喉咙里，皮肉被撕破；她突然彻底疯了，鲜血渗过了主堡塔楼的地板。

一天清晨，天还没亮，西蒙娜就来找我。她悲痛欲绝，也没带灯。“那本书受了诅咒，”她在黑暗中低声对我说，满脸都是泪。“伊莉丝，你不明白。我被永远困在埃尔西诺，困了一千年，甚至更久。我看遍了我能看到的每一种结局，这个世界每一种可能的模样，全都腐烂不堪。我能怎么办，伊莉丝？我能怎么办？那本书逼我选择，而我选择让阿斯特丽德和这一切一起腐烂，好让我掌权……”

她吻了我，向我道别，又把一枚钱币塞进我手里。“我躲不过上帝，”她说，“但我不能留在埃尔西诺。别告诉任何人我去了哪里。答应我，伊莉丝。”

而现在，我却在违背那个承诺。我知道西蒙娜还活着。多年前那个疯狂的星期里，究竟发生了什么？年幼的奥菲莉娅和雷欧提斯，还有我留下的心爱丈夫，往后会怎样？我到死都不会知道。

如果我的家人有一天读到这些，请记住：我这一生的幸运，远远超过了像我这样身份的女人所能奢望的。但在我的世界里，最幸运的事，始终是有你们。

source: Queen Gertrude's Diary
target: 乔特鲁德王后的日记

source:
May 2, MDXXXV

Tonight my husband seemed distressed. At first I thought he was missing our son, gone to Wittenberg. But... as the night progressed, he seemed to grow old before my eyes. He seemed... broken, somehow. When the second course was served, he collapsed while raising a toast—ironically, a toast to our health. I took him on my shoulders and bore him out of the great hall and up to his bedroom myself. 

As I lay him down in his bed, I noticed tears in his eyes. I tried to comfort him by kissing his forehead, but he pushed me away. "You will betray me," he rasped. "You will always betray me. Every time. You cannot do otherwise." 

He collapsed into something like sleep, then, and would not answer my questions.

When I returned to the party, our guests were concerned, but Claudius stepped in to assure them. "Everything's all right!" he boomed, in his loudest, most regal voice. "Everyone—Drink more! Don't take your health for granted!"

Then he turned and offered me his hand. "Now. I think a dance with the Queen will restore some life to this party. Don't you?" he said, smiling at me. It was as though I were the only woman in the whole world. In all my time married to Hamlet, he never once looked at me like that.

That evening, when all the guests had gone to bed, I found myself outside my bedroom door, saying my goodnights to Claudius.

"I don't want to go to bed," I told him, laughing. "I want the night to continue. Stop the dawn!"

"As you wish, my Queen," he said, and kissed me.

I was surprised at first. And yet—I wasn't. 

I kissed him back. He pulled my bedroom door shut behind him.

Surely I, too, deserve some happiness in this world that has been so cruel to me.

Don't I?
target:
MDXXXV年5月2日

今晚，丈夫似乎心神不宁。起初，我以为他在想念去了维滕贝格的儿子。但……随着夜色渐深，他仿佛在我眼前衰老了。他看起来……像是被什么击垮了。第二道菜端上来时，他正举杯祝酒，却倒了下去——讽刺的是，他祝的正是我们身体安康。我把他扛在肩上，亲自将他带出大厅，送上楼送进他的卧室。 

把他放到床上时，我发现他眼里有泪。我吻了吻他的额头，想安慰他，他却推开了我。“你会背叛我，”他声音嘶哑地说，“你永远都会背叛我。每一次。你做不到别的。” 

随后，他陷入了像是睡眠的状态，不再回答我的问题。

我回到宴会上时，宾客们都很担心，克劳狄斯却站出来安抚他们。“一切都好！”他用最洪亮、最有王者威严的声音说道，“各位——再多喝些！别把身体安康当成理所当然！”

接着，他转身向我伸出手。“来吧。我想，与王后共舞一曲，会让这场宴会重新热闹起来。你说呢？”他说着，朝我微笑。仿佛我是全世界唯一的女人。嫁给哈姆雷特这么久，他从未这样看过我，哪怕一次。

那晚，宾客们都去睡了，我站在自己的卧室门外，正向克劳狄斯道晚安。

“我不想睡，”我笑着对他说，“我想让这一夜继续下去。别让天亮！”

“遵命，我的王后。”他说，然后吻了我。

起初我很惊讶。然而——我又并不惊讶。 

我回吻了他。他随手关上了身后的卧室门。

这个世界对我如此残酷，我当然也该得到一些幸福。

难道不是吗？

source: The Ravings of King Hamlet
target: 哈姆雷特国王的疯言

source:
Again... again... again... Polonius, not even you can save your master from Hell this time.

I concede defeat on ever finding that book. The Hand of Dionysus, they call it. I find references, mentions, breadcrumbs. Did you know it's been mentioned as far back as Judas Iscariot, and even older still? Polonius, find the book so that no one must suffer, must die like this.

Time is nothing. Death is nothing. For the last hundred years alone I have lain in the garden, awaiting the trickle of my brother's poison in my ear a thousand times. Again and again and again. How cruel should it be that this gap of time seems to begin and end with me lying in the garden on a warm spring morning? How does my brother always find a way to kill me? Is his hatred of me truly so strong? And my wife—my wife, her faithfulness useless, meaningless, the bridal bed soiled with another's lust...

Let her have him if she loves him so much. Let them cavort in the halls of Elsinore, and some year hence, the chambers of Hell. I could not say goodbye to my only son. My regrets burn in my throat like acid, like poison. I can say goodbye only to you.

So farewell, my faithful advisor. Bury me far from Claudius if it's the last thing you do. I can hear the playmaster's foosteps in the hallway, here to relieve me from this endless madness. I give up. I give up.
target:
又一次……又一次……又一次……波洛涅斯，这一次，连你也救不了你的主人，让他免下地狱。

要找到那本书，我认输了。他们称它为“狄俄尼索斯之手”。我找到了一些记载、提及它的文字、零星的线索。你知道吗，早在加略人犹大的时代，就有人提到过它，甚至还要更早？波洛涅斯，找到那本书，让所有人都不必再这样受苦、这样死去。

时间算不了什么。死亡算不了什么。仅仅过去这一百年，我就已在花园里躺过一千次，等着弟弟的毒药滴进我的耳朵。一次又一次，一次又一次。这段时间竟以我在温暖的春日清晨躺在花园里为起点，又以此为终点，这该是何等残酷？为什么弟弟总能找到杀我的办法？他对我的恨，当真如此深吗？还有我的妻子——我的妻子，她的忠贞毫无用处，毫无意义，新婚的床榻被另一个人的欲望玷污……

她既然那么爱他，就让她得到他吧。让他们在埃尔西诺的厅堂里尽情嬉闹，再过些年，就去地狱的房间里继续。我没能向我唯一的儿子道别。悔恨灼烧着我的喉咙，像酸液，像毒药。我只能向你道别。

那么，永别了，我忠诚的顾问。哪怕这是你最后能做的一件事，也要把我葬在远离克劳狄斯的地方。我听见了戏剧大师在走廊里的脚步声，他来让我摆脱这无尽的疯狂了。我放弃了。我放弃了。

source: Hamlet's Personal Journal
target: 哈姆雷特的私人日记

source: June 6, MDXXXV Ophelia will not even look at me. My love for her means nothing now. And in the great hall, they rejoice my uncle's crowning, my father's proud form but a distant memory. If my uncle does not allow me to return to Wittenberg soon, I fear I will well and truly perish. August 8 That thing was not my father. It can't be. My father lies buried. But if it wasn't my father... what devil or evil spirit was it? Am I truly losing my mind? Was it real? Can I be certain it wasn't just a horrid dream? No, the others saw it too... even if they won't speak to me of it. My uncle cannot be trusted. Devils disregarded, there is yet something evil in him. I found the literature which Bernardo mentioned, tucked away in the gallery downstairs... it only confirms my suspicions. And yet... something in me keeps me from acting on it. What has stolen my courage?
target: MDXXXV年6月6日 奥菲莉娅连看都不愿看我一眼。我对她的爱，如今已毫无意义。大厅里，他们欢庆着叔父加冕，父亲那威严的身影却已成了遥远的记忆。如果叔父不尽快准许我回维滕贝格，我怕自己真的会死去。 8月8日 那个东西不是我的父亲。不可能是。我的父亲已埋在地下。 但如果那不是父亲……那又是什么魔鬼或邪灵？我真的正在发疯吗？那是真的吗？我能确定那不只是一场可怕的梦吗？不，其他人也看见了……即使他们不愿和我谈起它。 叔父不可信。即便不去管那些魔鬼，他身上也仍有邪恶的东西。我找到了贝尔纳多提过的文字，藏在楼下的画廊里……它只是进一步证实了我的怀疑。然而……我心里有什么东西，让我迟迟无法据此采取行动。是什么夺走了我的勇气？

source: Physician's Report, King Hamlet
target: 医师报告：哈姆雷特国王

source:
...His Highness passed away last night, and my autopsy was performed this morning. The condition of the body is intact, with no visible sign of struggle or trauma... it would seem His Majesty died peacefully.

...As to the cause of death, the thickening of his blood at first gives the indication of a snake bite. He was slumbering in his garden when discovered, and of course, it being summer, there is nothing suspicious about being bitten by a snake, though it is most regrettable...

...However, upon closer inspection of the curdled blood, I detected a faint smell unlike any I had ever conceived of. And the bite wound is unlike any snake I have yet seen... very odd. 

...I am declaring his death an unfortunate accident under uncommon circumstances.

……陛下于昨夜去世，我于今晨进行了尸检。遗体完整，未见明显的挣扎或外伤痕迹……看来陛下去世时很平静。

……至于死因，血液变稠，初步显示可能是蛇咬所致。他被发现时，正在花园里小睡。当然，时值夏季，被蛇咬伤并无可疑之处，尽管这十分令人痛惜……

……然而，仔细检查凝结的血液时，我闻到了一股淡淡的气味，与我所能想到的任何气味都不相同。而那处咬伤，也不像我见过的任何一种蛇造成的……十分古怪。 

……我判定，他的死亡是特殊情况下发生的不幸意外。

source: Flight of the Executioner
target: 刽子手的出走

source:
...And so it came to pass that the King of the Realm died one night, leaving his two sons behind. In this savage and warlike country, it was customary that whichever child inherited the crown for himself would immediately kill the others, eliminating further competition. However, these two brothers were twins, born within a scant few moments of one another. And so they brought the matter to High Executioner Selene.

They found her standing at the edge of the highest cliff in the kingdom, above the rolling and raging sea. 

"I am twenty seconds older than my brother," said the first prince. "Without any doubt at all, I am the rightful heir. Lady Selene, please cast my brother over this cliff immediately!" 

Lady Selene bound the second prince's hands and led him to the edge of the cliff. But the second prince sputtered, suddenly, "This is wrong! I may be younger, but my brother's body is weak and frail. He becomes sicker each day, and soon he may very well die. Then the Kingdom will be left with no heir at all! Don't kill me—kill him!"

Lady Selene paused to think a moment, then bound the first prince's hands, too.

The first prince spat with disgust. "My brother is a jealous imbecile!" Lady Selene wrapped a blindfold around his eyes.

The second prince stamped his foot. "My brother is a weakling and cannot see reason!" As with the first prince, the second prince, too, was soon blindfolded. Both of them continued to argue at the top of their lungs, screaming for the other one's demise.

Then the sound of Executioner Selene's fading footsteps caught their attention. "High Executioner, come back! You must kill my brother! I must be king! Where are you going?"

"I'm off to pour myself a flagon of wine and then pursue a career change to the next kingdom over, in that order," Selene replied. "Sounds like this one's gone a bit rotten. Good luck finding your way home with those blindfolds and binds on, lads."

The two men lunged at each other, unwilling to stand down. And the both of them went tipping over the edge, careening into the sea. The kingdom was none the worse for it, in the end.

……于是，一天夜里，这个王国的国王去世了，留下两个儿子。在这个野蛮好战的国家，按惯例，无论哪个孩子继承王位，都会立即杀死其他孩子，铲除日后的竞争者。然而，这两兄弟是双胞胎，出生只相隔短短片刻。因此，他们把这件事交给了首席刽子手塞勒涅。

他们找到她时，她正站在王国最高的悬崖边，下方是翻腾咆哮的大海。 

“我比弟弟早出生二十秒，”第一位王子说，“毫无疑问，我才是合法的继承人。塞勒涅女士，请立刻把我弟弟扔下悬崖！” 

塞勒涅女士绑住第二位王子的双手，把他带到悬崖边。可第二位王子突然结结巴巴地喊道：“这不对！我或许年纪小些，但我哥哥身体虚弱，弱不禁风。他一天比一天病得重，很可能不久就会死。到时，王国就一个继承人也没有了！别杀我——杀他！”

塞勒涅女士停下来想了一会儿，然后把第一位王子的双手也绑了起来。

第一位王子厌恶地啐了一口。“我弟弟就是个嫉妒成性的蠢货！”塞勒涅女士用布蒙住了他的眼睛。

第二位王子跺着脚。“我哥哥是个病秧子，根本不讲道理！”和第一位王子一样，第二位王子很快也被蒙住了眼睛。两人仍扯着嗓子争吵，尖叫着要对方去死。

这时，刽子手塞勒涅渐渐远去的脚步声引起了他们的注意。“首席刽子手，回来！你必须杀了我兄弟！我必须当国王！你要去哪儿？”

“我先去给自己斟上一壶酒，再到隔壁王国改行。就按这个顺序来。”塞勒涅答道，“看来这个王国已经有些腐朽了。小伙子们，你们蒙着眼、捆着手，祝你们还能找到回家的路。”

两个男人谁也不肯退让，猛地扑向对方。结果两人一起跌出了崖边，直坠大海。到头来，王国也没因此变得更糟。

source: Letter to His Majesty
target: 致陛下的信

source:
Your Highness,

Indeed as I am in your employ, it is my highest honor and duty to obey anything you might ask, including the neglect of your father's grave if you so wish. Still, might I ask why you desire this so strongly?

Alexander was a mighty ruler in his time. Whatever horrors he might have borne you and King Hamlet—may he rest in peace—are no more. In life we are cursed to continually remember the flaws of a man, but when viewed through the mirror of death, perhaps we might look upon such a man's flaws more kindly. The Lord smiles upon forgiveness for difficult men.

Nevertheless, I will continue to ensure his grave is not cleaned and no new gifts are laid there.

With all fidelity,

Alard the Groundskeeper

我既受雇于您，遵从您的任何吩咐，自然是我至高的荣幸与职责；若您希望如此，任您父亲的坟墓荒废也不例外。不过，容我冒昧一问，您为何如此执意这样做？

亚历山大在世时是一位强大的君主。无论他曾给您和哈姆雷特国王——愿他安息——带来怎样的苦难，如今都已过去。人在世时，总免不了反复记起一个人的过错；可透过死亡这面镜子再看，或许我们能更宽厚地看待那些过错。宽恕难以相处之人，是主所喜悦的。

尽管如此，我仍会确保无人清扫他的坟墓，也无人献上新的祭品。

忠心不渝，

园丁阿拉德

source: A Sonnet for Gertrude
target: 献给乔特鲁德的十四行诗

source:
My glass shall not persuade me I am old
So long as youth and thou are one of date.
But when in thee time's furrows I behold,
Then look I death my days should expiate.
For all that beauty that doth cover thee
Is but the seemingly raiment of my heart
Which in thy breast doth live, as thine in mine.
How can I then be elder than thou art?
O therefore, love, be of thyself so wary
As I, not for myself, but for thee will,
Bearing thy heart, which I will keep so chary
As tender nurse her babe from faring ill.
Presume not on thy heart when mine is slain;
Thou gav'st me thine not to give back again.

只要青春与你同龄，
镜子便休想劝我承认衰老。
可当我见时光在你脸上犁出沟痕，
便盼死亡为我的岁月作了结。
因为覆在你身上的一切美丽，
不过是我心披在外面的衣裳；
我的心住在你胸中，如你的心住在我胸中。

所以，爱人啊，请珍重你自己，
如我也会珍重自己，不为我，而为你；
我怀着你的心，必将悉心守护，
如温柔的乳母护着婴孩，免遭伤害。
若我的心已死，莫以为你的心仍可安然；
你将它给了我，便不是要我再归还。

source: A Letter For Her Majesty
target: 致王后陛下的信

source:
My Dearest Gertrude,

I hope this letter finds you in excellent health. Although I have not had the pleasure of your company in some years, I hope you will remember me fondly, Aunt, as I do you. I write to you with news of your sister, my most beloved Aunt Margaret.

Not one month ago, as one of her maids served a meal, the maid happened to drop a glass goblet, causing it to shatter. One of those shattered fragments entered Margaret's foot, and caused her to take gravely ill as the wound festered. Her physician recommended the limb be removed, and Margaret, then in good health, bade it be so. Yet on the very morning she was to undergo such a thing, she passed into the arms of God. You will be pleased to hear, I am certain, that the sacrament was administered in advance. May God rest her eternal soul.

I know that Margaret would have wanted you by her side in her final moments. Take comfort in the fact that she loved you dearly, and spoke of you often in her last few days.

Your faithful nephew,
Charles
target:
我最亲爱的乔特鲁德：

愿您收到这封信时身体康健。虽然已有数年未能有幸与您相聚，我仍希望，姨母，您能像我思念您一样，怀着温情记起我。我写信是要告诉您关于您姐妹的消息，她也是我最亲爱的玛格丽特姨母。

不到一个月前，她的一名女仆在上菜时不慎掉落了一只玻璃高脚杯，杯子摔得粉碎。一块碎片扎进了玛格丽特的脚，伤口溃烂，使她病情危重。她的医生建议截去那条腿，玛格丽特当时身体状况尚好，便同意了。然而，就在她将接受截肢的那天清晨，她投入了上帝的怀抱。我相信，得知她已事先领受圣礼，您会感到欣慰。愿上帝赐她永恒的灵魂安息。

我知道，玛格丽特一定希望您在她最后的时刻陪伴在侧。她深爱着您，在最后几天里也时常提起您，愿这能给您些许安慰。

您忠实的外甥，
查尔斯

source: 8 Signs Your Nobleman Is Treacherous
target: 贵族心怀不轨的八个征兆

source:
Have you often wondered at the true form and character of your lover? Pay careful mind: here are eight signs he's foe rather than friend! 

FIRST, within mere days of your acquaintance, he declares that if you 'call him but love, he'll be new baptis'd.' This nobleman is a walking source of dramatic show, clinging to any poor girl who crosses his path. Abnormally likely to meet his end in poison and tears.

SECOND, he uses the term 'taming' or 'shrew' in your presence—or even worse, in the same sentence. If he attempts to starve you to break your will, eat his heart out.

THIRD, he suddenly finds himself madly in love with your closest friend after promising you his undying heart. Keep a sharp eye out for faerie dust in the vicinity. 

FOURTH, he sticks a dagger in your back, then blames it on your 'ambition.' Don't worry: your restless spirit will have revenge. Stay indoors on March 15 if possible.

FIVE, after you help him murder his friends and cover up the crimes, he begins embarrassing you with inappropriate sobbing at your dinner parties. Even the most heartening prophecy can't revive this relationship. 

SIX, he tells you your wife has been unfaithful, but offers flimsy proof. Take a walk, enjoy some deep breathing, and stay away from pillows.

SEVEN, he tries to convince you to kill your brother. One might think this clear as day, yet this author is continually surprised.

EIGHT, sometimes he tells you to get to a nunnery. Other times he tells you he 'did love you once.' Which is it? Send this uncouth boy sulking back to university!
target:
你是否常常琢磨，恋人的真面目和品性究竟如何？请留个心眼：下面八个征兆，说明他是敌人，而非朋友！ 

第一，才认识几天，他就宣称，只要你“叫他一声爱人，他便重新受洗”。这位贵族浑身都是戏，见到哪个可怜姑娘都要纠缠一番。他死于毒药与泪水的可能性高得离谱。

第二，他当着你的面说起“驯服”或“悍妇”——更糟的是，把这两个词用在同一句话里。他若想靠饿着你来磨掉你的意志，那就把他的心挖出来吃掉。

第三，刚向你许下永不变心的誓言，他就突然疯狂地爱上了你最亲密的朋友。留意一下附近有没有仙子的魔法粉。 

第四，他在你背后捅了一刀，却说都是你的“野心”惹的祸。别担心：你不得安息的亡魂自会报仇。三月十五日，能不出门就别出门。

第五，你帮他杀害朋友、掩盖罪行之后，他却在你的晚宴上哭哭啼啼，失态得让你难堪。再鼓舞人心的预言，也救不了这段关系。 

第六，他说你的妻子对你不忠，却拿不出像样的证据。出去散散步，做几个深呼吸，别碰枕头。

第七，他试图说服你杀死自己的兄弟。这迹象似乎再明显不过了，可笔者仍一再为此感到惊讶。

第八，他一会儿叫你进修道院，一会儿又说他“曾经确实爱过你”。到底哪句才算数？把这个没教养的小子赶回大学，让他自己生闷气去！

source: The Cleric Butler
target: 教士管家

source: MARCH This morning I awoke from a vision of God as I slept. I saw Him before me in all His glory, and He spoke to me. When the dream faded, I realized my face was wet with tears. The Lord told me to enter the service of a certain Duke Iocus living in a town near here, and to oversee the man's baptism. This particular Duke was orphaned as a child, and as such, his holy education had been sorely neglected. I knew I had no choice but to obey God's will and to go seek out this man. That very dawn, I packed my things, paid the tab at my inn, and traveled over field and hill until I reached the gates of Duke Iocus's estate. Duke Iocus is a man of notorious reputation, to be certain; handsome, but wicked. Of course, as I have sworn a vow of modesty and chastity, I knew his wicked vices would have no influence on me. I knocked once and, hearing a shout, interpreted it as an invitation to enter. Imagine my surprise when I found the good Duke himself in the middle of beastly fornication with a young maiden... on the floor of the foyer, no less. The two of them were braying and sweating as nothing I'd ever seen. Flushing red, I coughed politely to make my presence known, but the Duke merely rolled over and lazily extended a hand in greeting. "Ahh, a cleric!" He boomed. "What brings you to my estate?" I introduced myself and declared my purpose to him, asking if he wished to be baptised. He roared with laughter. "What rubbish!" He explained to me that he had no need for a holy man, but all the need in the world for a stalwart butler... and so, before I could think of anything better, I agreed to serve him in that capacity. "I warn you, my new cleric butler," Iocus swore, "I shall never believe in any God you serve." He may say this now, but I believe I can change his heart. APRIL My lord Iocus has kept me busy this last month. One of my continual duties is to ensure the sanctity of his personal bedchamber, especially its cleanliness, so that he might continue to seduce all manner of impressionable young folk into it at all hours of the day and night. His lust seems to know no boundaries. I find it both frightening and some matter of clinical interest to me. Today, when tidying his chamber, I thought I might leave my bible at his bedside. Surely, I thought, he might read a page or two? I was right. He pushed into my room later that evening without knocking and handed the bible back to me. "What a fascinating book!" he declared. "Have you come to know God?" "Sort of. I read only the book called Song of Songs. I learned so many fascinating ways to compliment a woman's breasts. Never read anything so erotic in my life!" "And what of the rest of it, my liege?" He shrugged. "Dull. Dry. Lacking in action, heavy-handed on miracles to service the plot. Couldn't get through half of it without falling asleep." He spun on his heel and left. MAY For the last month, my lord Iocus kindly allowed me to bring a prayer group into his home. It is but once a week, on the sabbath. Tonight's subject was on preparing oneself to enter the communion of marriage and opening one's heart to God. Three young women and three young men came to our door, all of them in their finest clothing, ready to receive the Word. Ordinarily Iocus is prone to leaving home on nights like these to drink and play, but tonight he seemed compelled to linger. Not one hour in, after the wine had been served, Iocus came to me. "We've nothing to serve them to eat!" he fretted. "Nothing but bread and cheese. What sort of a meal is that? My good cleric, run into town and purchase an entire boar at once!" I donned my cloak, took a satchel of gold, and started off, giving the group my apologies. ...But three hours later, I returned to a scene which disturbed me to my core. Around the threshold of the front door were strewn half a dozen empty wineskins. Entering the foyer, I saw two of the young women giggling and chasing after the lads—all of them naked as babes and red in the face. From upstairs, I could faintly hear the sound of distant moans. "My Duke!" I called out. "What manner of sin is going on in this home?" Six voices rang out in muffled, sensual laughter. "What manner, indeed. I can be as specific as you like!" Duke Iocus called back, the seventh voice, barely stifling his own laugh. "Though we're, ah, preoccupied. Friends, make room in the bath—I'm coming in!" I think I must have gone into a dead faint, then. I knelt on the floor and prayed with all my might. Later that night, Iocus burst into my chambers. His hair was wild, his eyes rolling. He was stark naked. "Praise God!" He shouted. "I beg your pardon?" I said, bleary and half-awake. "My dear cleric, I've seen the light! I want you to baptise me immediately. Tomorrow at dawn, if possible!" "My lord," I said in shock, "What changed your mind?" Iocus shook his head. "I was nestled in a pile of limbs and lovemaking for hours. I thought for a moment I might die entwined like that. And I did experience a death, of sorts. But then, at the moment of release, a sense of utter peace came over me, the manner of which I can hardly describe. I've never felt so content! So magical! So right! I remembered all your endlessly dull lectures about the Holy Spirit. And I knew then that surely this must be your God's way of speaking through me. This must be how you feel every day!" I stared for a moment in horror. Neither of us spoke. "...So you'll be baptised?" I ventured after a long silence. "Right away, my good man. I want to be a Christian!" "Fair enough," I said, and went back to sleep. The Lord works in mysterious ways.
target: 三月 今晨，我从梦中上帝显现的异象里醒来。我看见祂在我面前，满身荣光，向我说话。梦境消散时，我才发现自己满脸泪水。主吩咐我去侍奉住在附近镇上的一位约库斯公爵，并负责为他施洗。这位公爵幼年便成了孤儿，因此，他的宗教教育被严重忽视了。我知道，我别无选择，唯有遵从上帝的旨意，去寻找此人。 就在那天黎明，我收拾好行李，结清旅店的账，穿过田野与山丘，直到来到约库斯公爵庄园的大门前。约库斯公爵确实声名狼藉；他相貌英俊，却品行邪恶。当然，我既已立下谦逊与贞洁的誓言，便知道他的邪恶恶习不会影响我。 我敲了一下门，听见一声喊叫，便当作是请我进去。想想我有多么吃惊吧：那位好公爵本人，竟正与一位年轻姑娘如野兽般交媾……而且就在门厅的地板上。两人嘶叫着，汗流浃背，那情形我从未见过。我满脸通红，礼貌地咳了一声，示意有人来了；公爵却只是翻了个身，懒洋洋地伸出一只手打招呼。“啊，一位教士！”他洪亮地说道，“什么风把你吹到我的庄园来了？” 我自报姓名，向他说明来意，问他是否愿意接受洗礼。他放声大笑。“一派胡言！”他向我解释，他不需要什么圣职人员，却急需一位尽职可靠的管家……于是，还没想到更好的办法，我就答应以管家的身份侍奉他。“我警告你，我的新教士管家，”约库斯郑重说道，“不管你侍奉什么上帝，我都绝不会信。” 他眼下或许这样说，但我相信，我能改变他的心意。 四月 过去这一个月，约库斯老爷让我忙得不可开交。我日常职责之一，就是确保他的私人寝室圣洁，尤其要保持干净，好让他日夜随时都能把各种容易受人影响的年轻人诱进房里。他的淫欲似乎毫无边界。我既觉得可怕，又从研究的角度对此有些兴趣。 今天收拾他的寝室时，我想，或许可以把我的《圣经》留在他床边。我心想，他总该会读上一两页吧？ 我猜对了。当天晚上，他没敲门便闯进我的房间，把《圣经》还给我。“真是本引人入胜的书！”他宣称。 “您已经认识上帝了吗？” “算是吧。我只读了那篇叫《雅歌》的。我学会了好多赞美女人胸脯的妙法。这辈子都没读过这么香艳的东西！” “那么其余的部分呢，老爷？” 他耸耸肩。“无聊。枯燥。没什么情节，倒是硬塞了不少奇迹来推动故事。还没读到一半就睡着了。”他转身便走。 五月 过去一个月，约库斯老爷好心允许我在他家中组织祈祷聚会。每周只有一次，就在安息日。今晚的主题是为步入婚姻的结合做好准备，并向上帝敞开心扉。三位年轻女子和三位年轻男子来到门前，个个都穿着自己最好的衣服，准备聆听圣言。通常这种晚上，约库斯总爱出门喝酒玩乐，可今晚他似乎忍不住要留下。 还不到一个小时，葡萄酒已经端上，约库斯便来找我。“我们没东西给他们吃！”他焦急地说，“只有面包和奶酪。这算哪门子饭？我的好教士，快进镇里去，立刻买一整头野猪回来！”我披上斗篷，带上一袋金币，向众人致歉后便出发了。 ……可三小时后，我回来所见的情景，却令我从心底感到不安。前门门槛四周，散落着六只空酒囊。走进门厅，我看见两位年轻女子咯咯笑着追逐那些小伙子——所有人都像初生婴儿一般赤裸，脸色通红。楼上传来隐约的呻吟声。 “公爵大人！”我喊道，“这屋里究竟在犯什么罪？”六个人发出低低的、充满情欲的笑声。 “究竟什么罪，这可问得好。你想听多详细，我都能说！”约库斯公爵回喊道，这是第七个人的声音，他自己也快憋不住笑了。“不过我们，啊，正忙着。朋友们，在浴池里腾个地方——我也来！” 我想，那时我一定已经昏厥过去了。我跪在地板上，用尽全力祈祷。 那天深夜，约库斯闯进我的寝室。他头发凌乱，眼珠乱转，全身赤裸。“赞美上帝！”他喊道。 “您说什么？”我睡眼惺忪，半梦半醒地问。 “亲爱的教士，我已看见了光！我要你立刻为我施洗。可以的话，就在明天黎明！” “老爷，”我惊愕地说，“是什么让您改变了心意？” 约库斯摇摇头。“我在交缠的肢体间温存了好几个小时。有那么一刻，我以为自己会就这样缠绕着死去。而我确实经历了一次死亡，某种意义上的。可就在释放的那一刻，一种无比安宁的感觉笼罩了我，我简直无法形容。我从没这么满足过！这么神奇！这么美好！我想起你那些关于圣灵的、没完没了的乏味说教。那时我便知道，这一定是你的上帝借我的身体传达旨意的方式。你每天一定都是这种感觉！” 我惊恐地瞪着他，一时无言。我们谁也没说话。沉默许久后，我试探着问：“……这么说，您愿意接受洗礼？” “立刻就来，我的好伙计。我要做个基督徒！” “那好吧。”我说完，便接着睡了。 主行事自有奥秘。

source: May Eve
target: 五月节前夜

source:
I remember Celeste rode in the front.

She was the head of the May parade, wearing a long white dress with a blue ribbon around her waist and flowers braided into her hair. No one had ever seen a May Queen half so pretty, they said. A trail of wagons tied together proceeded down the only street in town and there she sat at the very front, skirts trailing beneath her legs, which dangled off the wagon's edge. Her feet were bare and pale and clean, her eyes a blue to match her sash. And even I had to admit she was beautiful.

I watched her go by from just outside mum's cottage. She turned to smile at me and called out. 'Anna! Come dance with us!' She extended her hands towards me, the bells tied to her wrists tinkling faintly. We had been best friends once, after all.

But the boys who walked at her side jeered at me. 'Ugly little bitch!' one of them screeched. Another tossed a stone. 'Brown-toothed, slack-jawed, scruff-haired nothing!' One of them came after me with a stick, as though he meant to break it over my back.

Tears filling my eyes, I retreated into the woods. Far away from the raucous sounds of the May Day parade, everything here was dark and silent. The trees stretched like fingers overhead, and for a moment I forgot myself in that darkness. I knew not where I went, but walked with my eyes locked upon the mossy ground. There was no path. I needed none.

All humans know when they have truly become lost. And so I had. It was nearly midnight now, though it had been noon when I left my mother's threshold. A full moon lit my path, casting twining shadows on the forest floor. 

At last I came upon a still lake. And there I prayed to the spirit of spring herself, that great goddess whose image all May Queens were created in. 'Make me beautiful like Celeste,' I cried. 'Make me worthy of being the May Queen, too!'

The waters parted. A single wave lapped the surface. And then, slowly, the mare climbed out of the water's depths, one hoof at a time. It was a white mare, drenched through, and it shook its head wildly, flicking drops of water from its mane. Surely this must be the goddess herself, manifested in mortal form. Its mane was braided -- just as Celeste's had been -- but with mossweed, not flowers.

The mare stood before me, its golden eyes fixed upon me. At last it said (with no mouth that could move, but with a voice all the same) 'Child of man, have you come to seek my aid?'

'I have,' I said, quietly. 'I want to be beautiful. As beautiful as Celeste.'

It bowed its great head to me and nuzzled my hand. I touched it tenderly, its breath on my fingers. And, flooded with sudden relief that my prayer had been answered, I pressed my face into its mane and sobbed.

'Cry not, child of man,' it told me. 'Come into my dark waters and be reborn as a goddess in your own right. Merely climb on my back, and we'll descend together. You shall be a May Queen yet.'

I wrapped its mane round my fingers and pulled myself up her back with all my might, swinging one leg over her sinewy side. Together, we began to descend into the water. I felt the cold bite of it weighing down my skirts, my shoes; and before I knew it, the water was up to my chest. 

It was then I peered beneath the surface and my heart leapt into my chest. The mare was no mare, but a rotted, hulking thing, its flesh stripped in pieces from its corpse and fluttering in the water's current. The wet stink of death came upon me, and I gagged. I reached for the only thing I could grab -- a branch overhanging the pond -- and pulled with all my might. The creature ceased its descent beneath the water and turned upon me, its face little more than two shriveled eyes in a grinning skull.

A name rose to my lips, a choked scream. 'Brook horse!'

'Yesssss,' the thing in the water hissed. Its horselike lips pulled back, revealing sharpened teeth.

I turned to swim, but felt those teeth closing down upon my back. The moon grew small, high above the surface, fading from reach. The soft green of it all surrounded me. I sank down to the moss at the bottom. No. Not moss. Remains. And the last thing I saw was that sharp, grinning smile.

'You shall never be Queen,' it rasped. 'But your bones shall be beautiful indeed.'
target:
我记得塞莱斯特坐在最前面。

她领着五月节的游行队伍，身穿白色长裙，腰间系着蓝丝带，头发里编着鲜花。大家说，从没见过哪位五月女王有她一半漂亮。一辆辆相连的马车沿着镇上唯一的街道前行，她就坐在最前头，裙摆垂在腿下，双腿悬在车沿外。她光着脚，双脚白净，眼睛和腰间的丝带一样蓝。就连我也不得不承认，她很美。

我站在妈妈的小屋外，看着她经过。她转过头，对我微笑着喊道：“安娜！来跟我们一起跳舞吧！”她朝我伸出双手，系在手腕上的铃铛轻轻作响。毕竟，我们曾经是最好的朋友。

可走在她身旁的男孩们却嘲笑我。“丑八怪，小贱人！”其中一个尖声叫道。另一个扔来一块石头。“黄牙、呆脸、乱毛的废物！”还有一个拿着棍子朝我追来，像是要往我背上打，直到把棍子打断。

泪水盈满了我的眼睛，我退进树林。这里远离五月节游行的喧闹，一切都幽暗而寂静。树木像手指一样伸展在头顶，一时间，我在黑暗中忘了自己。我不知道自己去了哪里，只顾盯着长满苔藓的地面走。这里没有路。我也不需要路。

人真正迷路时，自己总是知道的。我就是如此。此时已近午夜，而我离开母亲家门时还是正午。一轮满月照着我前行，在林地上投下交错缠绕的影子。 

终于，我来到一片平静的湖边。我在那里向春天之灵祈祷，向那位伟大的女神祈祷——所有五月女王都是仿照她的形象装扮的。“让我像塞莱斯特一样美丽吧，”我哭喊道，“让我也配当五月女王吧！”

湖水分开了。一道波浪轻拍水面。接着，那匹母马缓缓从水底爬出来，一只蹄子接着一只蹄子。那是一匹白色的母马，浑身湿透，猛烈地甩着头，把水珠从鬃毛上甩落。这一定是女神亲自化作凡间的形体，显现在我面前。它的鬃毛也编成了辫子，和塞莱斯特的头发一样，只是编进去的是苔草，而不是鲜花。

母马站在我面前，金色的眼睛注视着我。终于，它开口了（它的嘴并不能动，却仍然发出了声音）：“人类的孩子，你是来向我求助的吗？”

“是的，”我轻声说，“我想变得美丽。像塞莱斯特一样美丽。”

它向我低下硕大的头，用鼻子蹭了蹭我的手。我轻柔地抚摸它，感受着它呼在我指上的气息。祈祷得到了回应，突如其来的宽慰涌上心头，我把脸埋进它的鬃毛里，抽泣起来。

“别哭，人类的孩子，”它对我说，“到我幽暗的水中来，重获新生，成为一位属于你自己的女神。只要爬上我的背，我们就一起下去。你终会成为五月女王。”

我把它的鬃毛缠在手指上，用尽力气爬上它的背，把一条腿跨过它筋肉结实的侧腹。我们一起开始向水中下沉。我感到刺骨的冷水浸透了裙子和鞋子，坠得它们沉甸甸的；还没反应过来，水就已经漫到了胸口。 

就在那时，我往水下看去，心猛地一跳。那母马根本不是马，而是一具腐烂的庞然巨物，尸身上的皮肉一片片剥落，在水流中飘动。湿腐的死亡恶臭扑面而来，我一阵干呕。我伸手抓住唯一够得着的东西——一根伸到池塘上方的树枝——拼命往上拉。那怪物停止了下沉，转头朝向我。它的脸几乎只剩下一颗咧嘴的骷髅头，嵌着两只干瘪的眼睛。

一个名字涌到嘴边，化作一声哽住的尖叫：“溪马！”

“是——啊——”水里的东西嘶声说道。它马一样的嘴唇向后掀起，露出尖利的牙齿。

我转身想游开，却感觉那些牙齿咬住了我的背。月亮在高高的水面上方越变越小，渐渐远得无法触及。四周柔和的绿色包围了我。我沉向水底的苔藓。不。那不是苔藓。是残骸。而我最后看见的，是那道尖牙毕露的狞笑。

“你永远成不了女王，”它嘶哑地说，“不过，你的骨头一定会很美。”

source: Walking The Low Beyond
target: 行于地下彼岸

source:
Hear me, young maidens who have traveled wild,
Whose eyes have never seen the touch of death,
Who tarry often when the sun grows dim,
Who linger long by cairns and caverns dark.

I once was you in spirit and in heart.
I am Persephone, the taken one.
When I was young I planted seeds alone,
And gathered flowers freely in the sun.

One day the earth burst forth with violent seams
And ashes belched with spite upon the land.
King Hades, Lord of Death, had come for me,
To seize and make me his unwilling bride.

At first I cried out to the world above,
But no one heard the call to grab my hand.
He pulled me down into the low beyond,
And I knew this was where I'd make my grave.

No flowers grew within the world of death.
I fell upon the ground and wept with fear.
As Hades offered me his outstretched hand,
I flinched from him and clenched my trembling fists.

He bade me then to take his hand's contents,
A small red fruit with tiny ruby seeds.
The god of many names, his countenance kind,
Pressed each small icy seed into my palm.

'Persephone, I'll never do you harm.
For years I've loved and watched you from afar.
Become my wife and you shall be the queen
Of everything that lives and moves about.

But if you wish to flee from me right now,
I'll trouble you no more and leave you be.
I brought you down here not to be your jailer,
But to show you the lands you might yet rule.'

Three days and nights I spent in Hades' world.
I grew to know his kingdom as my own.
When that third night fell on the river Styx,
I knew that I had made my final choice.

'I shall take these three seeds and be your bride,
If only you will grant me one small thing.
I wish to plant these seeds in darkness here,
And turn your endless winter into spring.'

So maidens, when you find you are now crones,
And when your kindest days all seem long past,
When winter sinks into your tired bones,
Prepare yourself to meet me then at last.

I'll guide you down the long unending halls
And bear you gently to the low beyond,
Where you will dine beside the ones you've lost
And join us in an everlasting bond.
target:
听我说，游历荒野的少女们，
你们的双眼尚未见过死亡，
常在日光渐暗时迟迟不归，
久久徘徊于石冢与幽暗洞穴旁。

我的心与灵魂也曾和你们一样。
我是珀耳塞福涅，被掳走的女子。
年轻时，我独自播下种子，
在阳光下自在地采集鲜花。

有一天，大地猛然裂开，
灰烬恶狠狠地喷涌，洒落大地。
冥王哈迪斯，死亡之主，为我而来，
要将我夺去，强娶为妻。

起初，我向地上的世界呼喊，
却无人听见，无人伸手拉住我。
他把我拉入地下的彼岸，
我知道，这里将是我的墓地。

死亡的世界里没有鲜花生长。
我倒在地上，恐惧地哭泣。
哈迪斯向我伸出手时，
我畏缩着躲开，攥紧颤抖的双拳。

随后，他让我接过掌中之物，
一颗红色的小果实，籽如细小的红宝石。
这位有着诸多名号的神，面容和善，
把一粒粒冰凉的种子放进我掌心。

“珀耳塞福涅，我绝不会伤害你。
多年来，我一直爱着你，从远处望着你。
做我的妻子，你便会成为女王，
统领一切活着、行走着的生灵。

但若你现在就想离我而去，
我便不再纠缠，任你离开。
我带你下来，并非要做你的狱卒，
而是让你看看将来或可统治的土地。”

我在哈迪斯的世界度过三天三夜。
渐渐熟悉他的王国，仿佛那是我的家园。
当第三个夜晚降临冥河斯堤克斯，
我知道，我已作出最后的选择。

“我愿收下这三粒种子，成为你的新娘，
只求你答应我一件小事。
我想把这些种子种在此处的黑暗里，
将你无尽的寒冬化作春天。”

所以，少女们，当你们也成了老妇，
当最美好的日子都仿佛远去，
当寒冬渗入你们疲惫的骨头，
就准备好，终于来与我相见吧。

我会引你们走过漫长无尽的厅堂，
轻柔地将你们带往地下彼岸，
在那里，你们将与逝去的亲人朋友同席，
与我们结下永恒的羁绊。

source: Ophelia
target: 奥菲莉娅

source: That's me. As the child of a duke, I have some small amount of standing—but as a daughter, I can inherit nothing. I've lived here at the castle all my life. Sometimes I dream about leaving... but where would I go, and what kind of life would I have? Everything I know about the world lies within Elsinore's walls.
target: 这就是我。身为公爵的孩子，我多少有些地位——但身为女儿，我什么也继承不了。我从小到大都住在这座城堡里。有时我会梦想着离开……可我能去哪儿，又能过上什么样的生活呢？我对世界的所有了解，都在埃尔西诺的城墙之内。

source: Hamlet
target: 哈姆雷特

source: Hamlet recently lost his father, the former King, who was also named Hamlet. He used to be very popular among those his age in Elsinore, with a much more cheerful disposition, but he's changed--and not for the better.
target: 哈姆雷特最近失去了父亲，也就是同样名叫哈姆雷特的先王。他过去在埃尔西诺的同龄人中很受欢迎，性情也开朗得多，可他变了——而且是变糟了。

source: Gertrude
target: 乔特鲁德

source:
The Queen is one of the kindest people I've ever met, and her people love her dearly. Gertrude isn't Danish, but married into the throne via her late husband, the King Hamlet. As is traditional, she remarried to the King's brother after his death—now she is Claudius's wife.

After my mother passed away when I was a child, Gertrude took Laertes and me under her wing. I've been eternally grateful to her for her kindness ever since.

Gertrude was born in Austria, and is a member of the illustrious Hapsburg family. In fact, her father is the Emperor Maximilian I. She's worked incredibly hard to learn Danish and eliminate her accent. I know she has a sister as well, who lives outside Denmark. Royal blood runs thick through her veins.
target:
王后是我见过最善良的人之一，她的子民都十分爱戴她。乔特鲁德不是丹麦人，而是嫁给已故的哈姆雷特国王后成为了王后。国王去世后，她依照传统改嫁给他的弟弟——如今，她是克劳狄斯的妻子。

我小时候母亲去世后，乔特鲁德便照顾起了雷欧提斯和我。从那以后，我一直感激她的善意。

乔特鲁德出生于奥地利，是显赫的哈布斯堡家族的一员。事实上，她的父亲就是马克西米连一世皇帝。为了学会丹麦语、消除口音，她付出了极大的努力。我知道她还有一个姐妹，住在丹麦以外。她的血脉里流淌着深厚的皇室血统。

source: Claudius
target: 克劳狄斯

source:
Claudius is the reigning King of Denmark. As the younger brother to King Hamlet, when Hamlet passed away, he inherited the throne. 

It's hard to get a read on him—he's too formidable for most to talk to directly. He seems comfortable in his power, and wields it well, though many find him arrogant and repulsive.
target:
克劳狄斯是丹麦现任国王。他是哈姆雷特国王的弟弟，在哈姆雷特去世后继承了王位。 

很难看透他——他威势太重，大多数人都不敢直接和他交谈。他似乎很适应手中的权力，也善于运用，尽管许多人觉得他傲慢又讨厌。

source: Polonius
target: 波洛涅斯

source: Polonius is my father, and the King's advisor. He can be a bit addle-brained at times, and he loves to talk—a lot—but he really just likes being around people, I think. He always means well. And he's been an attentive father to my brother Laertes and me... sometimes a little too attentive. It can be stifling.
target: 波洛涅斯是我的父亲，也是国王的顾问。他有时有点糊涂，而且特别爱说话——话多得很——不过，我想他其实只是喜欢和人待在一起。他总是出于好意。 他也一直很关心我哥哥雷欧提斯和我……有时候关心得有点过头了。让人喘不过气。

source: Laertes
target: 雷欧提斯

source:
Laertes is my brother, set to inherit the title of Duke when my father passes. He's set to travel all of Paris, learning his music and experiencing the world. Meanwhile... I'm here.

My brother means well, but sometimes he can be a little intense. He's quick to anger, and even faster to act impulsively. Hamlet hates him half to death, but other than that, he's friends with nearly everyone in Elsinore.
target:
雷欧提斯是我的哥哥，父亲去世后，他将继承公爵的头衔。他即将游遍巴黎，学习音乐，见识世界。而我……还在这里。

哥哥是好意，但有时候会有点过激。他很容易发怒，冲动行事更是快。哈姆雷特对他恨得要命，不过除此之外，他和埃尔西诺几乎所有人都是朋友。

source: Birgitta 'Brit' Brockenhuus
target: 比尔吉塔·“布莉特”·布罗肯胡斯

source:
Brit is Gertrude's lady-in-waiting. She can be terribly cruel. We've never gotten along since she came to Elsinore three years ago.

She is the daughter of one of the most powerful noble families in Denmark, as with most of the people here at Elsinore.
target:
布莉特是乔特鲁德的宫廷侍女。她有时刻薄得可怕。自从三年前她来到埃尔西诺，我们就一直合不来。

她出身于丹麦最有权势的贵族家族之一，和埃尔西诺这里的大多数人一样。

source: Bernardo
target: 贝尔纳多

source:
Sir Bernardo is Claudius's right hand man, and the most revered soldier in Elsinore. He doesn't say much, but he's been my friend since we were children.

He earned his merits as a young soldier in the most recent war with Norway, riding into battle alongside King Hamlet himself. After that, he quickly rose through the ranks to prominence, and he's even got the King's utmost respect.
target:
贝尔纳多爵士是克劳狄斯的得力助手，也是埃尔西诺最受敬重的军人。他话不多，但从小就是我的朋友。

在最近那场与挪威的战争中，他还是个年轻士兵，曾与哈姆雷特国王本人并肩驰骋沙场，立下战功。此后，他迅速晋升，声名鹊起，甚至赢得了国王极大的敬重。

source: Horatio
target: 霍拉旭

source:
Horatio is Hamlet's schoolmate from Wittenberg. From the look of him he can't be Danish, but I've never known his origin.

He served as a soldier in the last war alongside Bernardo, and from the way he carries himself he must be of noble birth, though exactly how I'm not sure. He's well-educated and eloquent, and always has something interesting to say.
target:
霍拉旭是哈姆雷特在维滕贝格的同学。看他的相貌，他不可能是丹麦人，但我从来不知道他来自哪里。

上一次战争中，他曾和贝尔纳多一起当兵。从他的举止来看，他一定出身贵族，至于具体是什么来头，我不清楚。他学识丰富，口才很好，说的话总是很有趣。

source: Irma
target: 伊尔玛

source:
Irma is one of the most feared women in Elsinore for her quick temper. She's fiercely devoted to the Queen, and originally followed Gertrude from Bohemia, where she and Gertrude were both born and raised.

Despite her teeth, I've seen that she has a warm side. She loves to gamble, and she's quite good; I wouldn't make a bet against her for all the world.
target:
伊尔玛脾气急躁，是埃尔西诺最让人畏惧的女人之一。她对王后忠心耿耿，当年从波希米亚随乔特鲁德来到这里。她和乔特鲁德都在那里出生、长大。

虽然她很厉害，我也见过她温暖的一面。她喜欢赌博，而且很有一手；说什么我也不会跟她对赌。

source: Marcellus
target: 马塞勒斯

source:
Marcellus has faithfully served Elsinore castle for several generations of royalty, and is a passionate advocate of the throne.

He's likely the oldest living man within its walls—he can be a little foggy at times, but years of practice with the sword have rendered him more capable than he seems.
target:
马塞勒斯忠心地为埃尔西诺城堡的几代王室效力，对王权拥护备至。

他很可能是城堡里年纪最大的男人——虽然有时有点糊涂，但多年的剑术练习让他的本事远胜于表面所见。

source: The Hand of Dionysus
target: 狄俄尼索斯之手

source: King Hamlet believes that if he had found a book - the Hand of Dionysus - he could have found a way to put an end to his plight. If this book exists, and is the source of this castle's curse, surely someone has to know something about it.
target: 哈姆雷特国王相信，如果他当初找到一本名为《狄俄尼索斯之手》的书，就能找到摆脱困境的办法。如果这本书存在，而且是城堡诅咒的源头，那一定有人知道些什么。

source: It seems clear this is the same book Quince had stolen from him long ago. If I can find it, then Quince might be able to offer some guidance on what to do with it next.
target: 看来很明显，这就是奎因斯很久以前从他那里偷走的那本书。如果我能找到它，奎因斯也许能指点我接下来该如何使用它。

source: Lady Simona was last seen with the Book of Fates, and I know something King Hamlet did not: She's still alive. I can find her. Someone who sees a great deal of people on a daily basis might know...
target: 西蒙娜女士最后一次被人见到时，带着《命运之书》。而我知道一件哈姆雷特国王不知道的事：她还活着。我能找到她。每天都见到很多人的人，也许会知道……

source: Othello says Simona has been living in Castle Town all along - her identity hidden, I suppose, but it's easier if no one even suspects they ought to be looking for you. She'll return to the bar on Sunday afternoon.
target: 奥赛罗说，西蒙娜一直住在城堡镇——我想，她隐瞒了身份，不过，如果根本没人想到要找你，藏身就容易多了。她会在星期天下午回到酒馆。

source: Othello told me Simona returns to castle town Sunday, but Fortinbras's invasion of Castle Town begins before I have a chance to meet her. How can I push back the invasion's onslaught? Surely there must be a way.
target: 奥赛罗告诉我，西蒙娜星期天会回到城堡镇，但还没等我有机会见她，福丁布拉斯就开始入侵城堡镇了。我该怎样推迟这场进攻？一定有办法。

source: I... found it. I possess the Book of Fates. So many pieces had to be moved in order for me to find it, but it now sits on my table. The book itself does not provide one exit, but many - and it seems Quince is far from who I thought he was.
target: 我……找到它了。《命运之书》已经在我手里。为了找到它，我不得不改变许多事情，但现在，它就在我的桌上。这本书提供的出路不止一条，而是许多条——看来，奎因斯也远不是我以为的那个人。

source: Prince Fortinbras's Threat
target: 福丁布拉斯王子的威胁

source: Fortinbras' offer of peace was a ruse. Elsinore comes to a violent end when he and his men storm the castle. But now that I know this is coming, surely there must be something I can do?
target: 福丁布拉斯提出议和只是个幌子。当他带人攻入城堡时，埃尔西诺便在暴力中走向终结。但现在我知道这一切即将发生，一定能做点什么吧？

source: Apparently Bernardo and Father have been convinced that Fortinbras posed a threat for months, but the King has been reluctant to act. They need more compelling evidence - some source close to Norway that could give me information.
target: 看来，贝尔纳多和父亲几个月来一直认定福丁布拉斯是个威胁，但国王迟迟不愿采取行动。他们需要更有说服力的证据——某个与挪威关系密切的消息来源，或许能向我提供情报。

source: With the help of Lady Brit, of all people, I was able to spy on Fortinbras in town and get the information I needed. I now know where in town the Prince is hiding. Perhaps Father or Bernardo could do something with this.
target: 没想到，帮我的竟然是布莉特女士。有她相助，我得以在镇上暗中监视福丁布拉斯，拿到了所需的情报。现在我知道王子藏在镇上的什么地方了。也许父亲或贝尔纳多能利用这个消息做点什么。

source: Fortinbras is in prison! If I give the War Council the information, Bernardo is able to find him and overwhelm him in town. As long as Norway's prince is in our hands, they won't dare mobilize against us. Could this actually work?
target: 福丁布拉斯入狱了！如果我把情报交给军事议事会，贝尔纳多就能在镇上找到他，将他制服。只要挪威王子在我们手里，他们就不敢调兵对付我们。这真的能行吗？

source: We almost had him! It seems if we suffer any losses, Fortinbras is able to take advantage of our internal disarray and escape. The invasion will still be delayed, but to stop it entirely... well, I'll simply need to keep everyone alive. Sounds deceptively straightforward.
target: 我们差一点就抓住他了！看来，只要我们有人丧命，福丁布拉斯就能趁内部混乱逃脱。入侵仍会推迟，但要彻底阻止它……嗯，我只需要让所有人都活下来。听着很简单，做起来可没那么容易。

source: I've... actually done it. The invasion has been held off, and everyone close to me survived! But it seems this is not a clean victory. The coming battles will drain on us and our nation. Is that worth it, to keep all my friends and family alive?
target: 我……真的做到了。入侵被挡住了，我身边所有亲近的人都活了下来！但看来，这场胜利并非没有代价。接下来的战斗会不断消耗我们和国家的力量。为了让所有亲友都活着，这样做值得吗？

source: The Melancholy of Lady Brit
target: 布莉特女士的忧郁

source: Brit has never been warm to me, but these days she seems especially down. I wonder if anyone has any ideas as to how I could reach her.
target: 布莉特从来没对我热情过，但这些天她似乎格外低落。不知道有没有人能帮我想想，怎样才能走近她。

source: When I saw Brit and Laertes meet, she told him something interesting: she's been divested of her artist's tools, and hasn't received a single letter from her mother. My brother proposed Horatio could help with the former, and Her Majesty with the latter.
target: 我看到布莉特和雷欧提斯见面时，她告诉他一件值得注意的事：她的绘画工具被拿走了，而且她连一封母亲的来信都没收到。哥哥提出，前一件事可以找霍拉旭帮忙，后一件则可以找王后陛下。

source: Horatio offered to help make new paints together in order to replace the ones that Brit used to have. Apparently he needs three components: charcoal, eggs, and linen. Pretty sure I can get some linen from my drawers, but I'll have to find a source for the other two.
target: 霍拉旭提出帮我一起制作新颜料，替代布莉特原来的那些。看来他需要三样东西：木炭、鸡蛋和亚麻布。我应该能从自己的抽屉里找到些亚麻布，但另外两样还得另找来源。

source: I can get charcoal from a fireplace, eggs from Irma's kitchen, and linen from my own dresser. With them, Horatio is able to make Brit a new set of paints!
target: 我可以从壁炉里拿到木炭，从伊尔玛的厨房拿到鸡蛋，再从自己的衣柜里拿到亚麻布。有了这些，霍拉旭就能为布莉特制作一套新颜料！

source: I can tell Laertes about Brit's situation, and he will agree to stay behind and check in on her. Hopefully, that meeting will go well.
target: 我可以把布莉特的情况告诉雷欧提斯，他会同意留下来，去看看她。希望这次见面能顺利。

source: Gertrude has been encouraging Brit to focus on her duties in the Castle, to the extent that she's been hiding letters from Brit's mother! She said something about 'where unheard wishes go.' What could that mean?
target: 乔特鲁德一直劝布莉特专心履行城堡里的职责，甚至藏起了布莉特母亲的来信！她提到什么“无人听见的愿望所去之处”。这是什么意思？

source: Gertrude hid letters from Brit's mother in the well in the grounds. Needless to say, Brit was not happy with them having been kept from her when I delivered them.
target: 乔特鲁德把布莉特母亲的来信藏在了庭院的井里。不用说，我把信交给布莉特时，她对这些信一直被瞒着的事很不高兴。

source: Unfortunately, it seems doing just one thing won't be enough to get Brit to open up to me. I'll have to figure out a couple different things to do.
target: 可惜，看来只做一件事，还不足以让布莉特向我敞开心扉。我得想想还能做哪几件不同的事。

source: I've succeeded. I had to perform a couple little acts of service, but I can sense that I'm getting to her. She said she plans head to the Castle Town bar, if I can catch her there, perhaps after we'll finally be able to talk.
target: 我成功了。我得帮她做几件小事，但能感觉到她开始接纳我了。她说她打算去城堡镇的酒馆，如果我能在那里遇见她，也许之后我们终于能好好谈谈。

source: Lost Notes, Now Ash
target: 遗失的笔记，如今已成灰

source: I saw Father burning some notes late at night in his room. What is he trying to hide?
target: 我看到父亲深夜在房间里烧一些笔记。他想隐瞒什么？

source: I've learned that by telling others about the burned documents, Father will be imprisoned, but I'm still no closer to learning about what those notes contain. I wonder if there's something I'm missing which might help me here.
target: 我发现，只要把焚烧文件的事告诉别人，父亲就会被关进监狱，但我还是一点也没弄清那些笔记里写了什么。不知道是不是有什么被我遗漏了，也许能帮我解开这个谜。

source: I met King Hamlet's ghost. King Hamlet's memories are fragmented, but he did give me a lead. My father is in possession of some notes, the King's last words, which contain some crucial but important knowledge. And although my father believes he must destroy them, the ghost claims he's wrong. Now that I know for certain that they were written by King Hamlet, that changes things.
target: 我见到了哈姆雷特国王的幽灵。他的记忆支离破碎，但还是给了我一条线索。父亲手里有一些笔记，是国王最后留下的话，其中记载着至关重要的信息。虽然父亲认为必须销毁它们，幽灵却说他错了。现在我确切知道这些笔记出自哈姆雷特国王之手，事情就不一样了。

source: The spirit says my father is in posession of his notes, and it's clear that these are the same notes my father will burn Thursday evening in his chambers. I have to find a way to stop them from being destroyed.
target: 幽灵说，他的笔记在我父亲手里。很明显，这正是父亲会在星期四晚上于房间里烧掉的那些笔记。我必须想办法阻止它们被销毁。

source: I had to do something truly monstrous in order to get my hands on the King's notes... but I found them nonetheless. Father will be safe and well in the next world. It doesn't make what happened right, but I know now his death is but a passing trial. Now all that's left is to speak to the ghost.
target: 为了拿到国王的笔记，我不得不做了一件骇人听闻的事……但我终究找到了它们。父亲在另一个世界会平安无事。这并不能让发生的事变得正当，但我现在知道，他的死只是一场暂时的考验。接下来，只剩下去和幽灵谈谈了。

source: A Missing Lute
target: 失踪的鲁特琴

source: I found a note from my brother discussing a lute he believes was stolen. He thinks Hamlet made off with it. Laertes and Hamlet have always had a contentious relationship, to say the least. I wonder if I can help resolve this situation.
target: 我找到了一张哥哥留下的字条，上面说他觉得有把鲁特琴被偷了。他认为是哈姆雷特拿走的。说得轻些，雷欧提斯和哈姆雷特一直处得很不愉快。不知道我能不能帮忙解决这件事。

source: As soon as Hamlet and Bernardo had a chance to meet, they quickly realized that the lute was lost, not stolen. They expect to spend some time over the next few days on a wild chase 'round the castle to find it.
target: 哈姆雷特和贝尔纳多一有机会见面，很快就弄清了：鲁特琴是丢了，并没有被偷。他们预计接下来几天要花些时间，把城堡到处找个遍，才能找到它。

source: They found the lute. I suppose I didn't realize how far Bernardo and Hamlet had drifted apart over the years, and how bad things had gotten between Hamlet and my brother. All this time, it seemed natural to assume we were no less close than we'd always been, but time changes things. I wonder if it's too late for Hamlet and my brother to make amends. If Laertes and Hamlet could only meet, I know something good might finally come of it.
target: 他们找到了鲁特琴。我想，我以前并没意识到，这些年来贝尔纳多和哈姆雷特已疏远到什么程度，也没意识到哈姆雷特和哥哥的关系已经变得多么糟糕。我一直自然而然地以为，我们还和从前一样亲近，但时间会改变许多事。不知道哈姆雷特和哥哥现在和好还来不来得及。只要雷欧提斯和哈姆雷特能见上一面，我知道事情也许终于会有好的转机。

source: Hamlet returned the found lute to Laertes. At first, Laertes was furious, but I think the conversation was many years in its formation. It seemed to be cathartic, in a way; they understand one another better now, at least. Perhaps I can leverage this to help them keep the peace in the future.
target: 哈姆雷特把找到的鲁特琴还给了雷欧提斯。起初，雷欧提斯很生气，但我想，这场谈话其实已经酝酿了许多年。某种程度上，他们似乎借此宣泄了积压的情绪；至少，他们现在更理解彼此了。也许我能借此帮助他们今后和睦相处。

source: Guildenstern is Dead
target: 吉尔登斯吞死了

source: Somehow Lady Guildenstern's gotten the idea that she could pretend to be dead, and she finds it rather funny. So funny, in fact, that she's asked me to tell everyone she really is dead. This can't end well.
target: 不知怎么，吉尔登斯吞女士想到了装死这个主意，还觉得挺有趣。她觉得这实在太有趣了，竟然让我告诉所有人，她确实死了。这肯定不会有好结果。

source: Rosencrantz, obviously heartbroken, planned Guilda's funeral as expected. At the very end, Guilda popped out and was... unpleasantly surprised at the lack of attendance. She's now decided that 'nothing matters' and 'we're all unimportant in the scheme of the universe' and other related nonsense. She's decided to plan a party for all of the other 'unimportant' folks in the castle and I'm invited. Insulting, yes, but I do like a good party.
target: 罗森克兰兹显然伤透了心，果然为吉尔达筹办了葬礼。到了最后，吉尔达突然冒出来，却因为没几个人到场而……大失所望。现在，她认定“什么都无所谓”“在宇宙之中，我们全都无足轻重”，还有诸如此类的胡话。她决定为城堡里其他“无足轻重”的人办一场聚会，我也受邀了。是有点侮辱人，不过我确实喜欢热闹的聚会。

source: I attended Guilda's little party, and at the end of it, I realized something horrible: She's going to die in earnest aboard that ship. They both are. And I have the power to save them. I can get on board and ensure Guilda lives. But first, I need to make sure I'm present when Hamlet and company sail for England on Saturday morning.
target: 我参加了吉尔达的小聚会。聚会结束时，我意识到一件可怕的事：她会在那艘船上真的死去。她们两个都会。而我有能力救她们。我可以上船，确保吉尔达活下来。但首先，我得保证星期六早上哈姆雷特一行启航去英格兰时，我就在场。

source: Guilda invited me to meet her on the foredeck. I wonder what she wants to discuss? Meanwhile, I need to find a way to avert this impending crisis.
target: 吉尔达约我在前甲板见面。不知道她想谈什么？与此同时，我得想办法化解这场迫在眉睫的危机。

source: I met Guilda on the deck, and there was a... moment, of sorts. I wonder, if we had more time together...
target: 我在甲板上见到了吉尔达，我们之间有了……某种特别的瞬间。我不禁想，如果我们能有更多时间相处……

source: I met Guilda on the deck, and she called me her 'good friend' for the first time. She might be the first true friend I've made in Elsinore recently.
target: 我在甲板上见到了吉尔达，她第一次称我是她的“好朋友”。她也许是我最近在埃尔西诺交到的第一个真正的朋友。

source: Guilda invited me to leave the castle with her and Rosencrantz forever. They want to gallivant around the countryside, selfishly forgetting and foregoing everything but their own worldly pleasure. Could I be happy, living such a life?
target: 吉尔达邀我和她、罗森克兰兹一起永远离开城堡。她们想在乡间四处游玩，自私地忘掉、舍弃一切，只顾自己享乐。过这样的生活，我能幸福吗？

source: The Spirit
target: 幽灵

source: Hamlet and others have seen a spirit of King Hamlet haunting the castle. This is how he learned of Claudius's deeds. If the ghost is indeed real, maybe there is a way for me to meet it. Surely Hamlet knows something.
target: 哈姆雷特和其他人都见过哈姆雷特国王的幽灵在城堡里徘徊。他就是这样得知克劳狄斯所做的事的。如果幽灵确实存在，也许我能找到办法见到他。哈姆雷特一定知道些什么。

source: Hamlet is tight-lipped on the spirit - he needs to be sure he can trust me. He's asked me to get information from a diary his mother keeps in her room. Well, if it's what must be done, then so be it.
target: 哈姆雷特对幽灵的事守口如瓶——他需要确定能信任我。他让我从他母亲放在房间里的日记中获取信息。好吧，如果非做不可，那就做吧。

source: I've obtained proof that Gertrude and Claudius's affair started before King Hamlet's death. If I let Hamlet know what I found, I'm certain he'll do something rash. But if that's what it takes to understand what's happening, perhaps it's wiser for me to follow this to its conclusion, no matter what.
target: 我拿到了证据，证明乔特鲁德和克劳狄斯在哈姆雷特国王去世前就开始了私情。如果我把发现告诉哈姆雷特，我确信他会做出冲动的事。但如果必须这样才能弄清到底发生了什么，也许更明智的做法就是无论如何都追查到底。

source: I've obtained proof that Gertrude and Claudius's affair started before King Hamlet's death. When I told Hamlet, he was fully consumed by his desire for revenge. He seems to have a plan he intends to execute during the time period when we would all ordinarily have gathered to watch Peter Quince's performance. I have a bad feeling about this, but if I want to meet this so-called ghost, I'll need to see this through to its end.
target: 我拿到了证据，证明乔特鲁德和克劳狄斯在哈姆雷特国王死前就有了私情。我把这件事告诉哈姆雷特后，他完全被复仇的欲望吞噬了。他似乎有个计划，打算在我们通常会聚在一起观看彼得·奎因斯演出的那段时间实施。我有种不好的预感，但如果我想见到这个所谓的幽灵，就得把这件事追究到底。

source: Some truly horrific acts occurred, but in the end, the spirit appeared. King Hamlet spoke to me. He waits on the walls each night at midnight. I've been asked to seek him out.
target: 发生了一些极其可怕的事，但最后，幽灵出现了。哈姆雷特国王和我说了话。他每晚午夜都会在城墙上等候。我被要求去找他。

source: Irma's Ire
target: 伊尔玛的怒火

source: Irma believes Hamlet is in need of some long-overdue discipline, and I've heard her grumbling to the Queen about it. There's no doubt that Hamlet's been difficult for everyone in Elsinore to handle. I wonder if I can force the issue to a resolution.
target: 伊尔玛认为哈姆雷特早就该好好管教了，我也听到她向王后抱怨这件事。毫无疑问，埃尔西诺的所有人都拿哈姆雷特没办法。不知道我能不能推动这件事得到解决。

source: I saw Hamlet and Irma meet, and the both of them fared worse for it. Hamlet was cruel and Irma only fed the flames. I sense something must come to a head sometime soon.
target: 我看到了哈姆雷特和伊尔玛见面，结果对两人都没好处。哈姆雷特言语刻薄，伊尔玛则只是在火上浇油。我感觉这场矛盾很快就会爆发。

source: I can hardly believe what came of all this. Irma poisoned Gertrude and Claudius to death. Not intentionally, of course; she was trying to eliminate Hamlet. But she was summarily thrown in the dungeon. I don't want to think about what Hamlet might do to her next, but I feel some obligation to see this horrible world run its course.
target: 我几乎不敢相信事情竟然变成了这样。伊尔玛毒死了乔特鲁德和克劳狄斯。当然，她并不是故意要杀他们；她原本想除掉的是哈姆雷特。但她随即被扔进了地牢。我不愿去想哈姆雷特接下来可能会怎么对待她，但又觉得自己有义务看着这个可怕的世界走到最后。

source: Irma's desire to discipline Hamlet ultimately degraded into a poisoning attempt which took the lives of the King, Queen, and herself. The people I love are capable of such horrors. It's frightening to think about. But I feel as though I understand a little better some of the tension bubbling just beneath the surface. And there's a possibility... that what happened here might help me, somehow, in the future.
target: 伊尔玛原本想管教哈姆雷特，最后却演变成了下毒谋杀，夺去了国王、王后和她自己的性命。我爱的人竟然能做出这么可怕的事。想想都让人害怕。但我似乎对表面之下涌动的种种矛盾多了一点了解。而且，这里发生的事……也有可能在将来以某种方式帮到我。

source: Claudius Coming Undone
target: 克劳狄斯的崩溃

source: King Claudius clearly holds a lot of power in Elsinore, but at a terrible cost: He killed his own brother. But what I don't know is why. What drives a man to do something like that? Maybe if I got to know the people close to him, I'd find out. It seems like the only person he trusts in the world is his wife, Queen Gertrude.
target: 克劳狄斯国王显然在埃尔西诺掌握着很大的权力，但代价惨重：他杀了自己的哥哥。可我不知道的是，为什么。究竟是什么让一个人做出这种事？ 也许多了解一下他身边的人，我就能找到答案。他在这世上唯一信任的人，似乎就是他的妻子，乔特鲁德王后。

source: Reading Gertrude's diary, I feel like I peered through a window into her relationship with the King. I get the impression Claudius has spent his entire life chasing Gertrude, his sole confidante and friend. Now, at last, he has her. I wonder what would happen if he didn't.
target: 读着乔特鲁德的日记，我觉得自己仿佛透过一扇窗，看到了她和国王之间的关系。在我看来，克劳狄斯一生都在追求乔特鲁德，她是他唯一的知己和朋友。如今，他终于得到了她。如果他失去了她，会发生什么呢？

source: Queen Gertrude passed away suddenly today. I noticed Claudius fled from the announcement. I wonder where he went off to.
target: 乔特鲁德王后今天突然去世了。我注意到，宣布这个消息时，克劳狄斯逃离了现场。不知道他去了哪里。

source: When I found Claudius, he was a sodden wreck, out of his mind with grief. And then he asked if I would stay with him as he slept. A duty his wife used to perform. I'm not sure I like where this is headed. Ought I to pursue the matter further? After all, I need only turn back the flow of time, and it'll be as though it never happened... for everyone but me, of course.
target: 我找到克劳狄斯时，他醉得一塌糊涂，悲痛得失去了理智。随后，他问我愿不愿意在他睡觉时陪着他。这原本是他妻子做的事。我不确定自己是否喜欢事情发展的方向。我该继续探究下去吗？毕竟，我只要让时间倒流，一切就像从未发生过一样……当然，对我以外的所有人来说是这样。

source: I agreed to visit Claudius in his private chambers. And at the end of the night, he made it clear—in no uncertain terms—that he desired to be with me. This is a man I've known since I was a child. It's hard to see him as anything other than Hamlet's uncle. But in his offer there was some implication about the kind of wealth the love of a King can bestow.
target: 我答应去克劳狄斯的寝室看他。那晚临别时，他说得再清楚不过：他想和我在一起。我从小就认识他。除了哈姆雷特的叔叔，我很难把他看作别的什么人。但他的提议也隐约暗示了，得到国王的爱能带来怎样的财富。

source: Claudius gave me a gift: an heirloom necklace. It's the finest thing I've ever worn, and I'm afraid to accept it. He means to make some grand romantic gesture soon, I think.
target: 克劳狄斯送了我一件礼物：一条传家项链。这是我戴过的最精美的首饰，我却不敢收下。我想，他很快就打算用某种盛大的方式表达爱意。

source: Claudius asked me to be Queen, and I consented. All this in a matter of days. Men in this family line seem to move unnaturally quickly when their hearts are similarly moved.
target: 克劳狄斯问我愿不愿意做王后，我答应了。这一切竟然只用了几天。这个家族的男人一旦动了这样的感情，行动似乎就快得异乎寻常。

source: Claudius and I underwent an official betrothal ceremony, to the utter surprise of everyone in Elsinore's court. In a scant few weeks, I'd be crowned Queen. I could rule this country, because the one who holds Claudius's heart holds all of him. Gertrude never used that power to her advantage... but I could. Is that right? More importantly, is that a future I want?
target: 克劳狄斯和我举行了正式的订婚仪式，埃尔西诺宫廷里的所有人都大吃一惊。再过短短几周，我就会被加冕为王后。我可以统治这个国家，因为掌握克劳狄斯的心，就掌握了他的全部。乔特鲁德从未利用这份力量为自己谋利……但我可以。这样做对吗？更重要的是，这是我想要的未来吗？

source: The Playmaster
target: 戏剧大师

source: I met an odd man named Peter Quince who seems to be a wandering actor of sorts. He's going to perform here in Elsinore Castle and has invited me to attend his performance.
target: 我遇到了一个名叫彼得·奎因斯的怪人，他似乎是个四处游历的演员。他准备在埃尔西诺城堡演出，并邀请我去观看。

source: Quince wishes to discuss something with me in private about his performances. His only requirement is that I've attended his play first, and then come to see him the morning afterwards in the Gallery.
target: 奎因斯想私下和我谈一些与他的演出有关的事。他唯一的要求是，我得先看过他的戏，再于第二天早晨去画廊见他。

source: Two things have become abundantly clear. The first is that Quince is outside the flow of time, as I am. And the second is that his plays are little more than cruel improvisation. He's decided to grant any request I might make regarding a subject for one of his plays. Judging by the reaction King Claudius had to the play about him, this might become useful to suss out more information from audience members.
target: 有两件事已经再清楚不过。第一，奎因斯和我一样，置身于时间流之外。第二，他的戏剧基本上只是残酷的即兴表演。他决定，无论我为他的戏提出什么题材，他都会接受。从克劳狄斯国王看那出关于自己的戏时的反应来看，这也许能帮我从观众身上探出更多信息。

source: I happened upon Quince in the gallery, where he and I exchanged a few words. He spoke to me about tragedy and referenced a tale I'd never heard about before. I don't know what to make of him. Is he teasing me or trying to help me, or both?
target: 我在画廊偶遇了奎因斯，和他聊了几句。他跟我谈起悲剧，还提到了一个我从未听过的故事。我不知道该怎么看待他。他是在戏弄我，还是想帮我，或者两者都有？

source: Quince performed a little side show in town, and it was odd, to say the least. If his story is to be believed, he's not only immortal, but some great godlike tool of his has been stolen from him. He's here in Elsinore to try and find it.
target: 奎因斯在镇上演了一出小戏，说得客气点，也实在古怪。如果他的故事可信，他不仅是不死之身，还被人偷走了一件拥有神一般力量的工具。他来到埃尔西诺，就是想找到它。

source: Quince visited me in my bedroom. He and King Hamlet's ghost are acquainted already. In fact, the both of them are outside the flow of time, like me. Quince claimed that I can find a way to stop the flow of time from repeating. But if so, how? The spirit must be connected.
target: 奎因斯来我的卧室找过我。他和哈姆雷特国王的幽灵早就认识。事实上，他们两个都和我一样，置身于时间流之外。奎因斯声称，我能找到办法，让时间不再反复循环。但如果真是这样，该怎么做？那个幽灵一定与此有关。

source: King Hamlet's final notes mentioned Quince as 'The Playmaster.' He writes that Quince 'relieved' him of his eternal torment, which explains why he's a spirit in my world and no longer trapped in time. But if Quince has the power to do that, why hasn't he done it for me? What's clear is that all paths seem to lead to me finding this book--this 'Hand of Dionysus.' I'll need to do that before I can understand more.
target: 哈姆雷特国王在最后的笔记中提到奎因斯，称他为“戏剧大师”。他写道，奎因斯让他从永恒的折磨中“解脱”了。这解释了为什么他在我的世界里是个幽灵，不再被困在时间之中。可如果奎因斯有这样的力量，为什么不对我这样做？ 有一点很清楚：所有的路似乎都指向找到那本书——那本《狄俄尼索斯之手》。我得先找到它，才能弄明白更多事情。

source: He lied to me. He's been lying to me this entire time. He's no friend of mine, and he's not here to help me. He tricked me into fetching this book from Simona for him, and then intended to deceive me into using it so that he can have it back.
target: 他骗了我。他一直都在骗我。他根本不是我的朋友，也不是来帮我的。他骗我替他从西蒙娜那里取来这本书，然后又打算骗我使用它，好让他拿回这本书。

source:
We did it. We killed him. We're free. We're really free. Is it over? It must be. I can hardly believe it.

The rest of my life begins today.
target:
我们做到了。我们杀了他。我们自由了。我们真的自由了。结束了吗？一定是结束了。我几乎不敢相信。

我的余生，从今天开始。

source: King Hamlet said it best: There will be no way out from this. The Playmaster cannot be defeated or outsmarted. This tragedy is inescapable. But within the confines that bind me, there is choice. That's all I have left to cling to.
target: 哈姆雷特国王说得最明白：这一切没有出路。戏剧大师无法被打败，也无法用计胜过他。这场悲剧无可逃避。但在束缚我的种种限制之内，我仍有选择。这是我仅剩的依靠。

source: Queen Astrid's Memory
target: 阿斯特丽德女王的往事

source: In various places, I've heard mention of Queen Astrid - Hamlet's grandmother - but I've realized I don't know much about her reign. I could ask around to learn more.
target: 我在不少地方听人提起过阿斯特丽德女王，也就是哈姆雷特的祖母，但我意识到，自己对她在位时的事所知甚少。我可以四处打听，多了解一些。

source: King Hamlet expressed to me that his mother, Queen Astrid, may have also experienced loops. I've grown up hearing so little about her and her legacy. There must be more to find.
target: 哈姆雷特国王告诉我，他的母亲阿斯特丽德女王可能也经历过时间循环。从小到大，我很少听人说起她和她留下的影响。一定还有更多事情等着我去发现。

source: If I talk to Father about Queen Astrid, he acts evasive. Evidently, the Queen was quite close to my mother, and he finds it painful to discuss her. He mentioned that he visits her grave Thursday night, though...
target: 只要我和父亲谈起阿斯特丽德女王，他就会回避这个话题。显然，女王和我母亲关系很亲近，而谈起她让父亲感到痛苦。不过，他提到自己会在周四晚上去她的墓前……

source: I've learned that my mother Elise kept an account of Astrid's story... and it might exist somewhere. My mother contracted plague and was sent away to die in a sanitarium off the southern coast, alone and frightened, by King Hamlet. After she perished, her belongings—along with those of other victims—were brought back by ship and sealed in a small shed near the docks. Perhaps I can learn more information there, if I can find a way in.
target: 我得知，母亲伊莉丝曾记录过阿斯特丽德的故事……那份记录也许还存放在某个地方。母亲染上瘟疫后，哈姆雷特国王将她送到了南部海岸外的一所疗养院，任她在孤独与恐惧中死去。她去世后，她的遗物和其他死者的遗物一起被船运了回来，封存在码头附近的一间小棚屋里。如果能找到进去的办法，也许我能在那里得到更多信息。

source: The tale of Queen Astrid turned out to be a complex one, involving her husband, his mistress, Simona, and... my mother. I got help retrieving my mother's belongings from the shack on the docks, and the notes she kept were... strange, to say the least. Simona was trapped in a loop as well, it seems, but what was this about a book? About choosing to be Queen? And could she really have escaped Elsinore alive?
target: 阿斯特丽德女王的故事远比想象中复杂，牵涉到她的丈夫、他的情妇西蒙娜，还有……我的母亲。有人帮我从码头的小屋里取回了母亲的遗物，而她留下的笔记……说得客气点，实在古怪。西蒙娜似乎也被困在时间循环里，可笔记里说的那本书是怎么回事？选择成为王后又是怎么回事？她真的有可能活着逃离埃尔西诺吗？

source: Gertrude's Chambers
target: 乔特鲁德的寝室

source: The door to Gertrude's chambers is locked - but I won't let that stop me. There has to be a way to get inside. Someone close to her must know, surely.
target: 乔特鲁德寝室的门锁着，但我不会就此罢休。一定有办法进去。她身边亲近的人肯定知道。

source: I've tried asking around about permission to enter Gertrude's chambers. It seems as though only Lady Brit and Irma have keys to enter at the moment.
target: 我试着四处询问怎样才能获准进入乔特鲁德的寝室。目前似乎只有布莉特女士和伊尔玛有开门的钥匙。

source: Brit agreed to lend me her key - if I set her up for a 'private rendezvous' with Hamlet. Well, if it's what I need to do, the task seems straightforward enough. I'll just try not to think about the consequences.
target: 布莉特答应把钥匙借给我，条件是我替她安排一次与哈姆雷特的“私下幽会”。好吧，如果非做不可，这件事看起来倒不难办。我尽量不去想后果就是了。

source: Irma tells me she would be willing to give me her key to Gertrude's room - if I organize a card game for herself, Lady Brit, Horatio, and Marcellus. I'll have to talk to each person she mentioned individually.
target: 伊尔玛告诉我，她愿意把乔特鲁德房间的钥匙给我，条件是我为她、布莉特女士、霍拉旭和马塞勒斯组织一场牌局。我得分别去找她提到的每个人谈谈。

source: Gertrude's private chambers are always locked when time resets, but now I know how to get inside. The key is hidden in the shrubbery outside the Queen's door - if I retrieve that key, I'll be able to enter freely from now on.
target: 每次时间重置，乔特鲁德寝室的门都会锁上，但现在我知道怎么进去了。钥匙就藏在王后门外的灌木丛里，只要拿到它，以后我就能自由出入。

source: To Catch A Spy
target: 揪出间谍

source: Bernardo suspects that there is a spy in Elsinore castle, stealing sensitive information and passing it on to unknown forces. I wonder who it could be.
target: 贝尔纳多怀疑埃尔西诺城堡里有个间谍，正在窃取机密情报，传给身份不明的势力。不知道那个人会是谁。

source: There is a spy in Elsinore Castle, and I have to find out who it is. If I cannot, then come Saturday morning, I die. But where would I start? Who could help me?
target: 埃尔西诺城堡里有个间谍，我必须查出那个人是谁。否则，到了周六早晨，我就会死。可我该从哪里查起？谁能帮我？

source: Bernardo is running his own investigation, interviewing people about what they know. If I send people to him, perhaps I could learn something by observing the meetings he has with them.
target: 贝尔纳多也在独自调查，向人们询问他们知道的情况。如果我让人去找他，也许能通过观察他们的会面了解到什么。

source: Someone has suggested my brother could help, but Laertes leaves for Paris early Thursday morning. I wonder if I could convince him to stay?
target: 有人说我哥哥或许能帮忙，但雷欧提斯周四一早就要动身去巴黎。不知道我能不能说服他留下？

source: I can convince Laertes to stay if I tell him of my fears before he leaves. I'm not sure what will come of it, but my brother is determined to unravel the potential threat. I should follow him.
target: 只要在雷欧提斯离开前告诉他我的担忧，我就能说服他留下。我不知道这会带来什么结果，但哥哥决心查清这个潜在的威胁。我应该跟着他。

source: Brit seems convinced that it is Claudius having me killed, because he finds my affection for Hamlet dangerous. It's believable, almost... but if Claudius wanted me dead, he's killed before, and wouldn't send another to do that work. Still, maybe there is something to find there.
target: 布莉特似乎认定，是克劳狄斯派人杀我，因为他觉得我对哈姆雷特的感情很危险。这几乎……说得通。可如果克劳狄斯想让我死，他以前就杀过人，不会派别人来做这件事。不过，也许这条线索还是值得查一查。

source: My efforts paid off. The spy, and my repeated killer, is Lady Brit. She's been in Norway's graces all along. I've got to find a way to expose her before she slits my throat again. Now I just have to stop her.
target: 我的努力有了回报。那个间谍，那个一次次杀死我的人，就是布莉特女士。她一直都深得挪威的信任。我得在她再次割开我的喉咙之前，想办法揭露她。现在只剩下阻止她了。

source: Lady Brit is apprehended, locked away in a cell by Bernardo. Does this mean I've successfully prevented my death? If I make it to Saturday night, I'll know I have.
target: 布莉特女士被捕了，贝尔纳多把她关进了牢房。这是否意味着我已经成功避免了自己的死亡？只要我活到星期六晚上，就能知道自己是否成功了。

source: By turning Lady Brit in to Bernardo, I managed to stop her from killing me this loop. It seems my success might be permanent - I was surprised by a visit from Quince, who promised me Brit would never come after my life again. How he intends to accomplish this, I'm unsure, but for now—I wonder what else lies before me.
target: 我向贝尔纳多告发布莉特女士，成功阻止了她在这次循环里杀我。这次成功似乎可能永久有效——奎因斯意外来访，向我保证布莉特再也不会来取我的性命。我不清楚他打算如何做到这一点，但眼下——我想知道，前方还有什么在等着我。

source: My Father's Death
target: 父亲之死

source: Bernardo just delivered the news: Father is dead. Hamlet killed him after the play Friday night. I... am having trouble processing, believing that it's true. There is so much I would have done differently if I had known this was how it was going to end. I'll miss you, Father.
target: 贝尔纳多刚刚带来了消息：父亲死了。星期五晚上演出结束后，哈姆雷特杀了他。我……还无法接受，也难以相信这是真的。要是早知道会是这样的结局，我有太多事会换一种做法。我会想念你的，父亲。

source: ...And yet, that wasn't the end after all. I'm back at the beginning again, in a time where Father is alive. I've never been so happy to have him berate me. Maybe I have a chance to change his fate! I know that he was killed in Gertrude's rooms, and that Hamlet committed the deed. Seems as good a place to start as any.
target: ……然而，那终究不是结局。我又回到了起点，回到了父亲还活着的时候。被他训斥，我从未这么高兴过。也许我有机会改变他的命运！我知道他是在乔特鲁德的房间里被杀的，凶手是哈姆雷特。看来就从这里查起也不错。

source: I decided to try the obvious and tell my father what I had seen. He found my warnings hard to believe, yet he seemed to take them into account anyway. Perhaps that will be enough to save him.
target: 我决定先试试最直接的办法，把自己看到的事告诉父亲。他觉得我的警告难以置信，但似乎还是放在了心上。也许这样就足以救他。

source: Though my father found my warnings disturbing, it doesn't seem telling him alone was enough to save him. Bernardo just informed me of his death - again. I need to know more about how the events played out - and find a way to change the state of that room.
target: 虽然我的警告让父亲感到不安，但看来光是告诉他，还不足以救他。贝尔纳多刚刚又告诉我，父亲死了。我需要进一步了解事情是如何发生的，并想办法改变那个房间里的状况。

source: If I can find a way to access Gertrude's private chambers, maybe I can know more about the events that led to my Father's death.
target: 如果我能想办法进入乔特鲁德的私人寝室，也许就能更清楚地了解导致父亲死亡的那些事。

source: I... I did it. I actually saved him. Though it did not come without a cost, it meant so much to me to see him live beyond a fate that previously seemed inescapable. I know it's a temporary victory - at the end of these days it will all be reset, and then he will probably die many times, just as before. But now... at least I know something can be done.
target: 我……我做到了。我真的救了他。虽然付出了代价，但看到他逃过那曾经似乎无法避免的命运，继续活下去，对我来说意义重大。我知道这只是暂时的胜利——这几天一结束，一切就会重置，他大概又会像以前那样，一次次死去。但现在……至少我知道，确实有办法改变这一切。

source: Prince Hamlet's Madness
target: 哈姆雷特王子的疯病

source: Hamlet showed up in my room, raving incomprehensibly. He's been difficult before, but this is strange even for him. What could be causing him to act out like this?
target: 哈姆雷特出现在我的房间里，胡言乱语，让人听不懂。他以前也难以相处，但即便是他，这样也太反常了。究竟是什么让他有了这样的举动？

source: I've been pointed towards the gallery—perhaps something exists there that could give me some clue as to the origin of Hamlet's recent bout of madness.
target: 有人指引我去画廊——也许那里有什么线索，能让我了解哈姆雷特最近发疯的缘由。

source: In the gallery, I found a clue as to Hamlet's madness. Apparently, he's been obsessing over some irregularities in his father's death report. Clearly, Hamlet suspects there is more to this story—but what is he hoping to accomplish?
target: 我在画廊找到了有关哈姆雷特疯病的线索。看来，他一直在纠结父亲死亡报告里的几处异常。显然，哈姆雷特怀疑这件事另有隐情——但他究竟想做什么？

source: It seems that Hamlet is concentrating most of his energy on putting on a play for this Saturday. Something's brewing. I feel uneasy about this.
target: 哈姆雷特似乎把大部分精力都花在了筹备本周六的演出上。他在酝酿什么。这让我感到不安。

source: Hamlet's actions and plans seem to have borne fruit—after the play, King Claudius confessed to God that he was the snake who killed Hamlet's father. The revelation was stunning, but Hamlet was strangely unsurprised... his actions indicate he already knew? Where could he have gotten his information?
target: 哈姆雷特的行动和计划似乎有了结果——演出结束后，克劳狄斯国王向上帝忏悔，承认自己就是杀死哈姆雷特父亲的那条毒蛇。这个真相令人震惊，可哈姆雷特竟然毫不意外……从他的举动来看，他早就知道了？他是从哪里得到消息的？

source: Hamlet's madness was brought on not by love, but by a meeting with what he believes to be the spirit of his father. It's from there he must have gotten his information about Claudius's murder. But the information turned out to be correct - so does this spirit actually exist?
target: 哈姆雷特发疯并非因为爱情，而是因为他见到了一个他认为是父亲亡魂的存在。他关于克劳狄斯杀人的消息，想必就是从那里得来的。但消息确实属实——难道这个亡魂真的存在？

source: The Barkeep and Me
target: 酒馆老板与我

source: Othello, the barkeep in town, seems to live in a world separate from mine. I'd like to observe what his day-to-day life might be like.
target: 镇上的酒馆老板奥赛罗，似乎生活在一个与我截然不同的世界里。我想看看他的日常生活是什么样的。

source: The inn in town has been the target of a group of thugs lately, who are trying to extort Othello for more and more money. The situation is untenable for Othello. If the Royal Guard were aware, they might be able to protect him.
target: 最近，一伙恶徒盯上了镇上的旅店，不断向奥赛罗勒索越来越多的钱。奥赛罗已经难以支撑下去。如果王家卫队知道了这件事，也许能保护他。

source: Othello has invited me to hear him tell stories... in private, after the bar is closed. I hardly think it's an innocent request, but I also find him respectful enough to feel safe seeing him alone. Father would be furious to know I'd gone without a chaperone, but... well, what he doesn't know can't hurt him, surely.
target: 奥赛罗邀请我听他讲故事……等酒馆打烊后，私下去听。我不太相信这只是个单纯的邀请，但他对我足够尊重，让我觉得独自见他也很安心。要是父亲知道我没有人陪同就去了，一定会大发雷霆。不过……嗯，只要他不知道，总不会让他难受吧。

source: Othello told me the most incredible tale, and when he was done, he asked me about Hamlet. I didn't know what to say. Not exactly. But then... we kissed, and it was incredible. It still gives me shivers to think about it. What does this mean for my relationship to him? More importantly, ought I to go and see him again tomorrow, as he requested?
target: 奥赛罗给我讲了一个精彩极了的故事，讲完后，他问起了哈姆雷特。我不知道该怎么说。也不完全知道。可后来……我们接吻了，那感觉美妙极了。现在想起来，我仍会浑身颤栗。这对我和他的关系意味着什么？更要紧的是，我该不该应他的邀请，明天再去见他？

source: Othello told me the most incredible tale, and when he was done, he asked me about Hamlet. I didn't know what to say. Not exactly. He asked me if he could kiss me, and I turned him away. I don't think I can think of him that way, at least not right now.
target: 奥赛罗给我讲了一个精彩极了的故事，讲完后，他问起了哈姆雷特。我不知道该怎么说。也不完全知道。他问能不能吻我，我拒绝了他。我想我没法对他抱有那样的感情，至少现在还不能。

source: Othello and I were together for the first time, in the woods. It was nothing like it was with Hamlet... he was gentle, but knew exactly what he was doing. It was the kind of quiet, intimate night I've rarely shared with another person, let alone someone unrelated to me. One of those nights when you feel as if you've known someone forever after just a few hours. Something large has shifted in our relation to one another. We were interrupted by Claudius. I've never been angrier in my life. How dare he try to tell me what's appropriate for me and what isn't? I'll do as I like, go where I will. Othello made it out unscathed, but I'm certain the experience frightened him. I ought to go see him as soon as possible.
target: 我和奥赛罗第一次亲热，是在树林里。那感觉和我与哈姆雷特在一起时完全不同……他很温柔，也很清楚自己在做什么。这样安静、亲密的夜晚，我很少与别人共度，更别说是没有亲属关系的人。有些夜晚就是这样，短短几个小时，就让你觉得仿佛认识了对方一辈子。我们之间的关系发生了很大的变化。克劳狄斯打断了我们。我这辈子从没这么生气过。他凭什么来告诉我，什么对我合适，什么不合适？我要做自己想做的事，去自己想去的地方。奥赛罗安然无恙地离开了，但我确信这件事吓到了他。我该尽快去看看他。

source: Othello and I went to the woods together, and I showed him the castle... or at least, the fringes of it. And he taught me to swim. It was the kind of quiet, intimate night I've rarely shared with another person, let alone someone unrelated to me. One of those nights when you feel as if you've known someone forever after just a few hours. We were interrupted by Claudius. I've never been angrier in my life. How dare he try to tell me what's appropriate for me and what isn't? I'll do as I like, go where I will. Othello made it out unscathed, but I'm certain the experience frightened him. I ought to go see him as soon as possible.
target: 我和奥赛罗一起去了树林，我带他看了城堡……至少是城堡的外围。他还教了我游泳。这样安静、亲密的夜晚，我很少与别人共度，更别说是没有亲属关系的人。有些夜晚就是这样，短短几个小时，就让你觉得仿佛认识了对方一辈子。克劳狄斯打断了我们。我这辈子从没这么生气过。他凭什么来告诉我，什么对我合适，什么不合适？我要做自己想做的事，去自己想去的地方。奥赛罗安然无恙地离开了，但我确信这件事吓到了他。我该尽快去看看他。

source: I found Othello and apologized. He asked me to run away with him, to leave Elsinore forever and travel south. Quince promised me Othello was 'fated to love another,' but that we'd enjoy a good life together until that time came. Maybe that's enough.
target: 我找到了奥赛罗，向他道了歉。他让我和他一起远走高飞，永远离开埃尔西诺，往南方去。奎因斯向我保证，奥赛罗“命中注定会爱上另一个人”，但在那一天到来之前，我们会一起过上美好的生活。也许这样就够了。

source: The Prince's Ambitions
target: 王子的抱负

source: Hamlet asked to meet me in private, and confided to me that he desires to 'prove his worth' to me and rekindle our relationship. First, though, he believes he must complete some 'dark work' of his own.
target: 哈姆雷特约我私下见面，向我坦言，他想向我“证明自己的价值”，让我们重拾旧情。不过，他认为自己得先完成一些“黑暗之事”。

source: The 'dark work' to which Hamlet refers is avenging his father's murder. He cannot rest, or become King, until that mission is complete. There are ways I could assist him... were I so inclined.
target: 哈姆雷特所说的“黑暗之事”，就是为被杀的父亲报仇。在完成这项使命之前，他无法安歇，也无法成为国王。我有办法帮他……如果我愿意的话。

source: Hamlet came to me after the news of his uncle's death was announced. He's done it. He's cleared all obstacles in his path to become King. But will he be able to successfully accomplish all it takes to be named the official heir? I can help him. I can ensure he has the right advice. The next few days shall be a critical window in which to act to determine the fate of the country as a whole, and of Hamlet's life.
target: 叔父的死讯公布后，哈姆雷特来找了我。他做到了。他扫清了成为国王的所有障碍。但要被正式指定为继承人，他能顺利完成所有必要的事吗？我可以帮他。我可以确保他得到正确的建议。接下来的几天将是采取行动的关键时机，整个国家的命运，以及哈姆雷特一生的命运，都将由此决定。

source: I told Hamlet I wanted to try again, with us. That things might be different this time. I truly believe, in my heart of hearts, that he's changed... but will it stay that way? What if he returns to the horrid person he's been all summer? I'll have to abandon him again, then, and I'm not certain what would come of it. But for now, I remain hopeful.
target: 我告诉哈姆雷特，我想和他重新试一次。这次也许会有所不同。我打心底里相信，他已经变了……可他能一直这样吗？要是他又变回这一整个夏天里那个可怕的人呢？那我就不得不再次离开他，而我不知道那会带来什么后果。但眼下，我仍抱着希望。

source: Hamlet asked me to marry him. To become Queen. I'd never dared to think about it before now. But I consented. I'm going to rule. And when I do, I'm going to do what dozens of queens before me could not. I know the cost of death. I know what it is to suffer. Under me, no one will suffer as I have. Never again.
target: 哈姆雷特向我求婚了。要我成为王后。在此之前，我从未敢想过这件事。但我答应了。我将统治这个国家。到那时，我要做到前几十位王后都没能做到的事。我知道死亡的代价。我知道受苦是什么滋味。在我的治下，不会有人再遭受我经历过的苦难。再也不会。

source: Hamlet lied to me. He told me he wanted to make me happy, to honor me... and now he's gone and banished Laertes and my father, believing them to be threats to his rule. Is this the cost of this world? Become Queen, but lose my family? What a rotten, horrid trick to play. Even so, they might be happier outside Elsinore. And far safer. Perhaps all is not lost.
target: 哈姆雷特骗了我。 他说，他想让我幸福，想尊重我……可现在，他竟然放逐了雷欧提斯和父亲，认为他们会威胁他的统治。这就是这个世界的代价吗？成为王后，却失去家人？这场骗局真是卑劣又可怕。 即便如此，离开埃尔西诺，他们也许会更快乐。而且安全得多。也许还不算失去了一切。

source: It appears to be the case that if I spurn Hamlet's advances, Queen Gertrude will ensure Brit and Hamlet are betrothed. What sort of world would it be, one where Lady Brit sits the throne? Perhaps it would behoove me to run this journey to its end and find out.
target: 看来，如果我拒绝哈姆雷特的追求，乔特鲁德王后就会促成布莉特与哈姆雷特的婚约。如果布莉特女士坐上王位，那会是怎样的世界？也许我该把这段旅程走到最后，看看结果。

source: ...And suddenly, my betrothal to Hamlet was formally announced. I think it came as quite the shock to everyone. This wedding is moving forward, at least in this world. Is this a world I would want to keep forever?
target: ……突然间，我与哈姆雷特的婚约就正式公布了。我想，这让所有人都大吃一惊。婚事正在推进，至少在这个世界里是如此。这是我想永远保留下来的世界吗？

source: A Journey At Sea
target: 海上之旅
