source: But years of idleness on that front—all in the interest of better dedicating myself to His Majesty—have run our coffers dry.
target: 可我多年没有打理那些产业——全是为了更好地效忠陛下——如今家中的钱财已经耗尽了。

source: I did not, my lady. I would be—er—honored, of course.
target: 我没有，夫人。当然，我会——呃——深感荣幸。

source: No, no, no—this cannot be! It cannot be real, can it?
target: 不，不，不——这不可能！这不可能是真的，对吧？

source: Help! Help, guards, he's run me through, but I—I—augh...
target: 救命！救命，卫兵，他刺穿了我，可我——我——啊……

source: And Ophelia—you know—I—it—
target: 还有奥菲莉娅——你知道——我——这——

source: You mean—Hamlet?
target: 你是说——哈姆雷特？

source: Soon enough. He—Hamlet—from my mouth, his voice shall speak. He... wished you to lead.
target: 很快。他——哈姆雷特——他的声音会借我的口说话。他……希望由你来领导。

source: Soon enough. He—Hamlet—from my mouth, his voice shall speak.
target: 很快。他——哈姆雷特——他的声音会借我的口说话。

source: It is a sleep which one has no memory of entering.
target: 那是一场睡眠，却不记得自己何时入睡。

source: It is not the sovereign Heaven we were promised, Bernardo. But it is a dreamless peace, and an untroubled one.
target: 那不是人们向我们许诺的至高天堂，贝尔纳多。但那是一份无梦、无忧的安宁。

source: Think carefully upon this, Ophelia.
target: 仔细想想这件事，奥菲莉娅。

source: You can never turn back.
target: 你再也无法回头。

source: Indeed. You always knew my heart best, Gerta.
target: 的确。你一直最懂我的心，格尔塔。

source: I am certainly not proud to lose everything I spent my life fighting for.
target: 失去我毕生为之奋斗的一切，当然不值得我骄傲。

source: I wish my son were strong enough to stand and fight.
target: 我希望我的儿子能足够坚强，挺身而出，奋起抗争。

source: Hail the brother you killed.
target: 向你杀死的兄弟致意吧。

source: You cannot escape the eye of Heaven, brother.
target: 你逃不过上天的眼睛，弟弟。

source: I came not to bring peace, but to bring a sword.
target: 我来不是带来和平，而是带来刀剑。

source: And now you have murdered my son. My only child. My greatest treasure.
target: 如今，你又谋杀了我的儿子。我唯一的孩子。我最珍贵的宝物。

source: Look upon me. Did Christ not say, 'Surely I am with you always'? As am I with you... my black touch descends on your sullied court...
target: 看着我。基督不是说过：“我必常与你们同在”吗？我也与你同在……我的黑暗之触降临在你污秽的宫廷……

source: How strange and peculiar that you and I should meet now, at the end of time, at the end of this world.
target: 你我竟在此刻相遇，在时间的尽头，在这个世界的尽头，何其奇异，何其古怪。

source: Find me on the first night. You are too late for this fragment to exist. It will soon melt.
target: 第一夜来找我。你来得太晚，这个碎片已无法继续存在。它很快就会消融。

source: Ophelia. You must keep her safe.
target: 奥菲莉娅。你必须保护好她。

source: But I haven't. And my head—is screaming at me that the world would be better off without me.
target: 可我没有。而我的脑海——正向我嘶喊，说这世界没了我会更好。

source: Come no closer. Stay, my sweet. Stay in the world of the living.
target: 别再靠近了。留下来，亲爱的。留在活人的世界里。

source: Ophelia, plead some sense with her!
target: 奥菲莉娅，快劝劝她，让她清醒一点！

source: This is but one fragment.
target: 这只是一个碎片。

source: A thousand times I've seen her die. Not once has it been less easy to bear.
target: 我已见过她死去一千次。没有一次比之前更难承受。

source: You must save her, Ophelia. Save her from her pain.
target: 你必须救她，奥菲莉娅。让她摆脱痛苦。

source: S-She's strange! It's not just me! Everyone thinks so! H-how could you—
target: 她、她就是很古怪！不只是我这么想！大家都这么想！你、你怎么能——

source: Finally, some peace and—
target: 终于能清静一会儿——

source: I'm sorry. I'm so sorry, Ophelia. But everything you've been saying—these visions—
target: 对不起。真的对不起，奥菲莉娅。可你一直说的那些事——那些幻象——

source: I'm sorry. I'm so sorry. But everything you've been saying—these visions—
target: 对不起。真的对不起。可你一直说的那些事——那些幻象——

source: (Laertes is—)
target: （雷欧提斯——）

source: Who are you talking t—
target: 你在跟谁说——

source: No. No, it's not done. H-his face is—it's—
target: 不。不，还没结束。他、他的脸——那——

source: I—I have you not—and yet I see you still—
target: 我——我抓不住你——却依然看得见你——

source: It is a knell. It summons you to Heaven—or to Hell.
target: 那是丧钟。它召你去天堂——或去地狱。

source: I know I cannot stop you. So please—just be safe.
target: 我知道我拦不住你。所以，求你——一定要平安。

source: Lord Polonius? But he's long been faithful to both of my husbands—and to me. It cannot be!
target: 波洛涅斯大人？可他多年来一直忠于我的两任丈夫——也忠于我。这不可能！

source: You're—you want me to—leave Denmark forever?
target: 你——你想让我——永远离开丹麦？

source: T-that was—What I just did—
target: 那、那是——我刚才做的事——

source: These notes—
target: 这些笔记——

source: A-and—she's not like me. I might be cruel to her, but... she's a good person!
target: 而、而且——她跟我不一样。我对她也许很刻薄，可……她是个好人！

source: It feels as if something's—
target: 感觉好像有什么——

source: If something worse had happened, I—
target: 要是出了更糟的事，我——

source: I've got to attend to His Majesty—but please don't overtax yourself. I beg of you.
target: 我得去侍奉陛下了——但请别太勉强自己。求你了。

source: That is the summary of it, yes.
target: 是的，大致就是这样。

source: Consider your options carefully, Ophelia.
target: 仔细考虑你的选择，奥菲莉娅。

source: Life in place of death is not always a gift. You and I know that truest of all.
target: 以生代死，并不总是恩赐。你我比任何人都明白这一点。

source: After Father's death, when I tried to end my life, when I frightened you—I've been thinking ever since then that I wish I'd succeeded.
target: 父亲去世后，我曾试图结束自己的生命，吓到了你——从那以后，我一直在想，要是当时成功了就好了。

source: Ow! Stop! All right, point—made—Bernardo. Stop!
target: 哎哟！住手！好吧，我——明白了——贝尔纳多。住手！

source: This—Laertes—you don't know how sweet these words are to hear from you.
target: 这——雷欧提斯——你不知道，听你说出这些话，我有多高兴。

source: Of course, one might reason they'd woken up in the night with a sudden powerful thirst for a mug of wine, but—it seems unlikely.
target: 当然，也可以说他们半夜醒来，突然特别想喝一杯葡萄酒，可——似乎不太可能。

source: Above all, he is my dearest, truest friend—though he might be going through the darkest time of his life right now.
target: 最重要的是，他是我最亲密、最真诚的朋友——尽管他现在可能正经历着一生中最黑暗的时刻。

source: And—did you ever, with Hamlet...
target: 那——你有没有和哈姆雷特……

source: These rumors I've heard—about you, about these... 'theater performances?'
target: 我听到的那些传闻——关于你，还有那些……“戏剧演出”？

source: I edited the timeline—for your benefit, I might add—by telling Lady Brit just one little thing.
target: 我只告诉了布莉特女士一件小事，就修改了时间线——顺便说一句，这可是为了你好。

source: Quickly—I must bandage it. You. Fetch me cloth.
target: 快——我得包扎一下。你。给我拿块布来。

source: You—you can't call that 'besting' anything!
target: 你——这怎么能叫“战胜”了什么！

source: Ah! I've finally been struck with something. This must be Prince Hamlet—the romance you mentioned earlier!
target: 啊！我总算想到点什么了。一定是哈姆雷特王子——你之前提过的那段恋情！

source: Ha! I've only lived here two years. No, Ophelia—I am Somali, and was sold into slavery as a child.
target: 哈！我在这里才住了两年。不是的，奥菲莉娅——我是索马里人，小时候被卖作奴隶。

source: Though he trades in deception, he speaks one truth.
target: 他虽以欺骗为业，却说对了一件事。

source: This world guarantees a short but true happiness.
target: 这个世界能给你短暂却真实的幸福。

source: Most live life without ever experiencing such a thing. I certainly did. So shall many of these good people before us.
target: 大多数人终其一生都不曾体验过这样的幸福。我便是如此。我们面前的这些好人，许多也会如此。

source: Do not underestimate the power of a few good years to transform the course of your life...
target: 不要小看几段美好年华的力量，它们足以改变你的一生……

source: ...Even if those good years are certain to end.
target: ……即使那些美好的岁月注定会结束。

source: Most ordinary folk choose love not knowing where the future might lead.
target: 大多数普通人选择去爱时，都不知道未来会走向何方。

source: Quince has cursed you with this knowing. He's poisoned you. And he knows it.
target: 奎因斯让你知晓未来，以此诅咒了你。他毒害了你。而他自己清楚这一点。

source: But your feelings for Othello, and his for you, are written on both of your faces.
target: 但你对奥赛罗的感情，还有他对你的感情，都写在你们各自的脸上。

source: If you choose this world, go into it gladly. Do not let the inevitable pain rob the intensity of your love.
target: 如果你选择这个世界，就欣然走进去。别让不可避免的痛苦夺走你爱的热烈。

source: Or surely, the Playmaster will have won in the end.
target: 否则，最后赢的就一定是戏剧大师。

source: Ah—a large brown hare.
target: 啊——一只棕色的大野兔。

source: I thought that made her a peaceful child. I remember marveling to the doctor—'isn't she a wonder, my quiet child?'
target: 我以为这说明她是个安静的孩子。我记得自己还惊喜地对医生说——“我这安静的孩子，是不是很了不起？”

source: The first time I used the Book's power to kill, I was so very frightened—but that was so very long ago.
target: 第一次用那本书的力量杀人时，我怕得要命——可那已经是很久很久以前的事了。

source: Without so much as laying a hand on her victim's body. It was—it should have been impossible.
target: 她甚至没有碰过受害者的身体。这——这本该是不可能的。

source: I saw the murder. It was—it was my sister.
target: 我看到了那场谋杀。是——是我的姐妹。

source: She killed 'em without even touching 'em. S-she's—there's something wrong wiv' 'er.
target: 她连碰都没碰他们，就把他们杀了。她、她——她有点不对劲。

source: Ophelia—she—killed someone without even laying her hands on them. I saw her myself.
target: 奥菲莉娅——她——连碰都没碰那个人，就把人杀了。我亲眼看见她这么做的。

source: Those bodies you've heard about by now—I saw one of the murders wiv' my own eyes.
target: 那些尸体，你现在应该听说了吧——其中有一场谋杀，是我亲眼看见的。

source: Lady Ophelia killed 'em without even touching 'em. S-she's—there's something wrong wiv' 'er.
target: 奥菲莉娅女士连碰都没碰他们，就把他们杀了。她、她——她有点不对劲。

source: What happened—was that—was that real?
target: 怎么回事——那是——那是真的吗？

source: A-and were you—are you—are you going to kill us all?
target: 那、那你刚才是——你是——你要把我们全杀了吗？

source: I won't. Whatever I felt for you—watching all this—it's too much.
target: 我不肯。不管我曾经对你有什么感情——看着这一切——我实在承受不了。

source: If that her breath will mist or stain the stone—
target: 若她的气息能让这石头蒙上雾气、留下痕迹——

source: No. Something else. Whoever's in there—whatever you are.
target: 不。是别的东西。不管里面是谁——不管你是什么。

source: Fight back? You mean—kill Ophelia?
target: 反击？你是说——杀了奥菲莉娅？

source: Just—be prepared to take swift action if it comes to that.
target: 只是——做好准备，真到了那一步，就立刻行动。

source: I—find your offer intriguing. I think that would ease Father's spirit, knowing I was preparing to take his place.
target: 我——对你的提议很感兴趣。我想，父亲知道我正在准备接替他，也会感到宽慰。

source: And Mother, her life—she was caught up in all this.
target: 还有母亲，她的一生——她也被卷进了这一切。

source: These last few days have been—these last few months have been a living hell.
target: 这几天简直——这几个月简直如同活在人间地狱。

source: Never say that. If I could choose my own fate—it's always been you, Ophelia. You know that.
target: 别再这么说。如果我能选择自己的命运——我选择的始终是你，奥菲莉娅。你知道的。

source: This world belongs to the living.
target: 这个世界属于活着的人。

source: We are merely passing through, here only for this singular moment in time.
target: 我们只是过客，只在这独一无二的片刻停留。

source: Ophelia. Would that I could offer you the embrace of love a father-in-law ought to have for his daughter.
target: 奥菲莉娅。但愿我能给你一个满怀慈爱的拥抱，如公公对待自己的女儿那样。

source: My son... the darkness which unfolded within him in these past months has been buried, but not truly forgotten.
target: 我的儿子……过去几个月里，他心中滋生的黑暗已被埋藏，却并未真正被遗忘。

source: And someday, it shall rise up again to lash against you both.
target: 总有一天，它会再度涌起，伤害你们两人。

source: Can you be prepared for that eternity? Can you love him despite that, knowing it has hurt you before?
target: 你能准备好永远面对这一切吗？明知它曾伤害过你，你仍能爱他吗？

source: Think on that before you decide his fate, and yours.
target: 在决定他和你自己的命运之前，想清楚这一点。

source: You have already acted on the best advice I might give—to marry well, and quickly.
target: 我能给你的最好建议，你已经照做了——嫁个好人家，而且尽快成婚。

source: We had hoped to make such a match with Lady Brit, of course. But no longer. Still—
target: 当然，我们原本希望能和布莉特女士结成这样的姻缘。现在已经不作此想了。不过——

source: I—I know it is the birthright of a King that he have a Queen beside him.
target: 我——我知道，国王身边有一位王后，是他与生俱来的权利。

source: It is strange, how these matters bear forth.
target: 世事如此发展，真是奇妙。

source: You are a source of myriad surprises. I would never have anticipated this.
target: 你总能带来种种意外。这件事，我绝不会预料到。

source: It is not my place to pass judgement on this union. Nor is it Gertrude's, in the end.
target: 我无权评判这段结合。说到底，乔特鲁德也无权评判。

source: After all, this is not our world any longer.
target: 毕竟，这已经不再是我们的世界。

source: It belongs to the living. To you.
target: 它属于活着的人。属于你。

source: Ah, but who would want me dead? I can only—
target: 啊，可谁会想要我死呢？我只能——

source: If yeh'd asked me before now, I'd have said—I'll probably see what ransom I can get for the lot o' ye.
target: 要是你早些问我，我大概会说——我会看看拿你们这帮人能换多少赎金。

source: It is tempting to flee responsibility for the lives of those you love.
target: 逃避对所爱之人生命的责任，确实很诱人。

source: I sought to do the same.
target: 我也曾想这么做。

source: No man or woman could lay blame with you.
target: 无论男女，都不能因此责怪你。

source: But I fled, and I have spent every moment of consciousness since regretting the world I chose.
target: 但我逃了。从那以后，每一个清醒的瞬间，我都在为自己选择的世界后悔。

source: Whatever you choose—whatever fate you grant yourself—do not forget that you must live dreaming of the faces you left behind.
target: 不管你如何选择——不管你给自己怎样的命运——别忘了，今后你仍须活下去，梦里会有那些被你留下的面孔。

source: There's another option, too. If I can save Father's life—perhaps I can keep them both safe from further harm.
target: 还有另一个选择。如果我能救下父亲的命——也许就能保护他们两人，不再受到伤害。

source: It's true now more than ever. Even if—
target: 现在比以往任何时候都更是如此。即使——

source: I— think I could make something good and useful of myself, had I lived. But I'll never know for sure.
target: 我——觉得如果我还活着，也许能成为一个善良、有用的人。可我永远没法知道了。

source: Certainly. But I'd need some—
target: 当然。不过我需要一些——

source: —Eggs, charcoal, and linen.
target: ——鸡蛋、木炭和亚麻布。

source: What kind of—she just—ugh. I wish I could... speak to her about this. To ask her why. But I can't even do that, can I?
target: 这算什么——她就这样——唉。我真希望能……跟她谈谈这件事。问问她为什么。可我连这都做不到，是吗？

source: But she—I—we loved each other.
target: 可她——我——我们曾经相爱。

source: Oh—my head hurts—
target: 哦——我的头好痛——

source: Still—whatever he was planning has been delayed, at least.
target: 不过——不管他原本打算做什么，至少现在被拖延了。

source: All this—I feel like I'm going mad.
target: 这一切——我觉得自己快疯了。

source: What? But I thought Father was—
target: 什么？可我以为父亲已经——

source: I—if that's what I must do.
target: 我——如果我必须这么做的话。

source: I need—some time to think about it.
target: 我需要——一点时间想想。

source: His body was found at the foot of the walls. He was—
target: 他的尸体是在城墙下发现的。他——

source: Is this—did he use it on—Hamlet?
target: 这是——他用它对付了——哈姆雷特？

source: How did they discover my location? Did you—
target: 他们怎么知道我在哪里？是不是你——

source: But I also know—or suspect—that you are not someone who collapses under his grief.
target: 但我也知道——或者说，我想——你不是会被悲痛压垮的人。

source: I—I have. But I am afraid, in my heart of hearts.
target: 我——是的。但在内心深处，我很害怕。

source: I—I have. But something happened to him recently. I don't know that he even sees me when he looks at me, right now.
target: 我——是的。但他最近出了些事。现在他看着我的时候，我都不知道他是否真的看见了我。

source: Then—don't carry this alone. Let me carry it with you.
target: 那就——别独自承担。让我和你一起承担。

source: I—I suppose I could. This place holds no meaning to me anymore without him.
target: 我——想我可以。没有他，这个地方对我已经没有意义了。

source: I see. Excellent. I have something to—ah—to discuss with you.
target: 明白了。很好。我有件事要——啊——和你商量。

source: One of Grace's lieutenants. Staunchly loyal, I imagine—no sense trying to persuade him of much.
target: 格蕾丝的一名副手。我想，他一定忠心耿耿——试图说服他改变什么，恐怕没用。

source: Before today, I didn't even dare to dream that she might accept me—that we could be together.
target: 今天之前，我连想都不敢想，她会接受我——我们能在一起。

source: But your brother is an amazing man. And—for what it's worth—I think you and he are cut from the same cloth.
target: 但你哥哥是个了不起的人。而且——不管这话有没有用——我觉得你和他是同一类人。

source: Ah. you can still see me.
target: 啊。你还能看见我。

source: My son cannot see me any longer. He seems to have no memory of ever meeting me.
target: 我儿子已经看不见我了。他似乎完全不记得自己曾见过我。

source: ...It's for the best that way. They're happier, each of them.
target: ……这样最好。他们每个人都更快乐了。

source: Perhaps some outstanding task of mine still remains. I know not.
target: 也许我还有什么未竟之事。我不知道。

source: Either way, let us enjoy the world we have built, you and I. The others will never understand.
target: 无论如何，让我们享受这个由你我共同创造的世界吧。其他人永远不会明白。

source: Excellent work, Ophelia.
target: 做得很好，奥菲莉娅。

source: Do you still—did Claudius—kill your father?
target: 你还——克劳狄斯是不是——杀了你父亲？

source: (He seems to think—his father died of plague?)
target: （他似乎认为——他的父亲死于瘟疫？）

source: Still—he seems happy.
target: 不过——他看起来很快乐。

source: Fortunately for you, this is real as can be—and we're missing the party.
target: 你很幸运，这一切千真万确——而我们正错过宴会呢。

source: I've been—it's been—I've watched you all die so many times.
target: 我一直——这些日子——我已经看着你们所有人死去太多次了。

source: Is that—cheering?
target: 那是——欢呼声？

source: Please, Ophelia, flee now!
target: 求你了，奥菲莉娅，快逃！

source: This is all wrong. It's all—
target: 这一切都不对。全都——

source: Yes. And when one of them pulled my hair and said it looked odd—
target: 是的。后来，他们中有个人扯我的头发，说它看起来很奇怪——

source: Hand of Dionysus
target: 狄俄尼索斯之手

source: Our apologies, but there was an unexpected error that prevented the game from continuing and it must exit.
target: 很抱歉，发生了意外错误，游戏无法继续，必须退出。

source: Abandon current timeline and revisit the event that cemented this fate?
target: 放弃当前时间线，回到决定这一命运的事件？

source:
I remember Celeste rode in the front.

She was the head of the May parade, wearing a long white dress with a blue ribbon around her waist and flowers braided into her hair. No one had ever seen a May Queen half so pretty, they said. A trail of wagons tied together proceeded down the only street in town and there she sat at the very front, skirts trailing beneath her legs, which dangled off the wagon's edge. Her feet were bare and pale and clean, her eyes a blue to match her sash. And even I had to admit she was beautiful.

I watched her go by from just outside mum's cottage. She turned to smile at me and called out. 'Anna! Come dance with us!' She extended her hands towards me, the bells tied to her wrists tinkling faintly. We had been best friends once, after all.

But the boys who walked at her side jeered at me. 'Ugly little bitch!' one of them screeched. Another tossed a stone. 'Brown-toothed, slack-jawed, scruff-haired nothing!' One of them came after me with a stick, as though he meant to break it over my back.

Tears filling my eyes, I retreated into the woods. Far away from the raucous sounds of the May Day parade, everything here was dark and silent. The trees stretched like fingers overhead, and for a moment I forgot myself in that darkness. I knew not where I went, but walked with my eyes locked upon the mossy ground. There was no path. I needed none.

All humans know when they have truly become lost. And so I had. It was nearly midnight now, though it had been noon when I left my mother's threshold. A full moon lit my path, casting twining shadows on the forest floor. 

At last I came upon a still lake. And there I prayed to the spirit of spring herself, that great goddess whose image all May Queens were created in. 'Make me beautiful like Celeste,' I cried. 'Make me worthy of being the May Queen, too!'

The waters parted. A single wave lapped the surface. And then, slowly, the mare climbed out of the water's depths, one hoof at a time. It was a white mare, drenched through, and it shook its head wildly, flicking drops of water from its mane. Surely this must be the goddess herself, manifested in mortal form. Its mane was braided—just as Celeste's had been—but with mossweed, not flowers.

The mare stood before me, its golden eyes fixed upon me. At last it said (with no mouth that could move, but with a voice all the same) 'Child of man, have you come to seek my aid?'

'I have,' I said, quietly. 'I want to be beautiful. As beautiful as Celeste.'

It bowed its great head to me and nuzzled my hand. I touched it tenderly, its breath on my fingers. And, flooded with sudden relief that my prayer had been answered, I pressed my face into its mane and sobbed.

'Cry not, child of man,' it told me. 'Come into my dark waters and be reborn as a goddess in your own right. Merely climb on my back, and we'll descend together. You shall be a May Queen yet.'

I wrapped its mane round my fingers and pulled myself up her back with all my might, swinging one leg over her sinewy side. Together, we began to descend into the water. I felt the cold bite of it weighing down my skirts, my shoes; and before I knew it, the water was up to my chest. 

It was then I peered beneath the surface and my heart leapt into my chest. The mare was no mare, but a rotted, hulking thing, its flesh stripped in pieces from its corpse and fluttering in the water's current. The wet stink of death came upon me, and I gagged. I reached for the only thing I could grab—a branch overhanging the pond—and pulled with all my might. The creature ceased its descent beneath the water and turned upon me, its face little more than two shriveled eyes in a grinning skull.

A name rose to my lips, a choked scream. 'Brook horse!'

'Yesssss,' the thing in the water hissed. Its horselike lips pulled back, revealing sharpened teeth.

I turned to swim, but felt those teeth closing down upon my back. The moon grew small, high above the surface, fading from reach. The soft green of it all surrounded me. I sank down to the moss at the bottom. No. Not moss. Remains. And the last thing I saw was that sharp, grinning smile.

'You shall never be Queen,' it rasped. 'But your bones shall be beautiful indeed.'

我记得塞莱斯特坐在最前面。

她领着五月节的游行队伍，身穿白色长裙，腰间系着蓝丝带，头发里编着鲜花。大家说，从没见过哪位五月女王有她一半漂亮。一辆辆相连的马车沿着镇上唯一的街道前行，她就坐在最前头，裙摆垂在腿下，双腿悬在车沿外。她光着脚，双脚白净，眼睛和腰间的丝带一样蓝。就连我也不得不承认，她很美。

我站在妈妈的小屋外，看着她经过。她转过头，对我微笑着喊道：“安娜！来跟我们一起跳舞吧！”她朝我伸出双手，系在手腕上的铃铛轻轻作响。毕竟，我们曾经是最好的朋友。

可走在她身旁的男孩们却嘲笑我。“丑八怪，小贱人！”其中一个尖声叫道。另一个扔来一块石头。“黄牙、呆脸、乱毛的废物！”还有一个拿着棍子朝我追来，像是要往我背上打，直到把棍子打断。

泪水盈满了我的眼睛，我退进树林。这里远离五月节游行的喧闹，一切都幽暗而寂静。树木像手指一样伸展在头顶，一时间，我在黑暗中忘了自己。我不知道自己去了哪里，只顾盯着长满苔藓的地面走。这里没有路。我也不需要路。

人真正迷路时，自己总是知道的。我就是如此。此时已近午夜，而我离开母亲家门时还是正午。一轮满月照着我前行，在林地上投下交错缠绕的影子。 

终于，我来到一片平静的湖边。我在那里向春天之灵祈祷，向那位伟大的女神祈祷——所有五月女王都是仿照她的形象装扮的。“让我像塞莱斯特一样美丽吧，”我哭喊道，“让我也配当五月女王吧！”

湖水分开了。一道波浪轻拍水面。接着，那匹母马缓缓从水底爬出来，一只蹄子接着一只蹄子。那是一匹白色的母马，浑身湿透，猛烈地甩着头，把水珠从鬃毛上甩落。这一定是女神亲自化作凡间的形体，显现在我面前。它的鬃毛也编成了辫子，和塞莱斯特的头发一样，只是编进去的是苔草，而不是鲜花。

母马站在我面前，金色的眼睛注视着我。终于，它开口了（它的嘴并不能动，却仍然发出了声音）：“人类的孩子，你是来向我求助的吗？”

“是的，”我轻声说，“我想变得美丽。像塞莱斯特一样美丽。”

它向我低下硕大的头，用鼻子蹭了蹭我的手。我轻柔地抚摸它，感受着它呼在我指上的气息。祈祷得到了回应，突如其来的宽慰涌上心头，我把脸埋进它的鬃毛里，抽泣起来。

“别哭，人类的孩子，”它对我说，“到我幽暗的水中来，重获新生，成为一位属于你自己的女神。只要爬上我的背，我们就一起下去。你终会成为五月女王。”

我把它的鬃毛缠在手指上，用尽力气爬上它的背，把一条腿跨过它筋肉结实的侧腹。我们一起开始向水中下沉。我感到刺骨的冷水浸透了裙子和鞋子，坠得它们沉甸甸的；还没反应过来，水就已经漫到了胸口。 

就在那时，我往水下看去，心猛地一跳。那母马根本不是马，而是一具腐烂的庞然巨物，尸身上的皮肉一片片剥落，在水流中飘动。湿腐的死亡恶臭扑面而来，我一阵干呕。我伸手抓住唯一够得着的东西——一根伸到池塘上方的树枝——拼命往上拉。那怪物停止了下沉，转头朝向我。它的脸几乎只剩下一颗咧嘴的骷髅头，嵌着两只干瘪的眼睛。

一个名字涌到嘴边，化作一声哽住的尖叫：“溪马！”

“是——啊——”水里的东西嘶声说道。它马一样的嘴唇向后掀起，露出尖利的牙齿。

我转身想游开，却感觉那些牙齿咬住了我的背。月亮在高高的水面上方越变越小，渐渐远得无法触及。四周柔和的绿色包围了我。我沉向水底的苔藓。不。那不是苔藓。是残骸。而我最后看见的，是那道尖牙毕露的狞笑。

“你永远成不了女王，”它嘶哑地说，“不过，你的骨头一定会很美。”

source: Gertrude was born in Austria, and is a member of the illustrious Hapsburg family—in fact, her father is the Emperor Maximilian I. She's worked incredibly hard to learn Danish and minimize her accent entirely. I know she has a sister as well, who lives outside Denmark. Royal blood runs thick through her veins.
target: 乔特鲁德出生于奥地利，是显赫的哈布斯堡家族的一员——事实上，她的父亲就是马克西米利安一世皇帝。她为学习丹麦语、尽可能彻底消除口音付出了极大的努力。我知道她还有一个姐妹，住在丹麦以外。她的血脉中有着深厚的王室渊源。

source:
Irma is one of the most feared women in Elsinore for her quick temper. She's fiercely devoted to the Queen, and originally followed Gertrude from Bohemia, where she and Gertrude were both born and raised.

 Despite her teeth, I've seen that she has a warm side. She loves to gamble, and she's quite good; I wouldn't make a bet against her for all the world.
target:
伊尔玛脾气急躁，是埃尔西诺最让人畏惧的女人之一。她对王后忠心耿耿，当年从波希米亚随乔特鲁德来到这里。她和乔特鲁德都在那里出生、长大。

虽然她很厉害，我也见过她温暖的一面。她喜欢赌博，而且很有一手；说什么我也不会跟她对赌。

source: Grace and I spent the night together. I hope I see her again soon—or perhaps, if there's a way out of this repeating world, that I might accept her offer to sail the world.
target: 格蕾丝和我共度了一夜。希望很快能再见到她——或者，如果有办法离开这个不断重复的世界，也许我能接受她的邀请，航遍世界。

source: When I found Quince in the gallery, he spoke in riddles. Something about the nature and structure of a tragic work. Of course I've read many of the great tragedies—and it sometimes feels like I'm living one—but what does all that have to do with my predicament?
target: 我在画廊找到奎因斯时，他说话像在打哑谜。说的似乎是悲剧作品的本质和结构。我当然读过许多伟大的悲剧——有时也觉得自己正身处一出悲剧之中——但这一切和我的困境有什么关系？

source: Marcellus has thirteen children, and grandchildren at that. I had no idea he was so—er—prolific. Then again, having to raise thirteen children would explain why nothing fazes him.
target: 马塞勒斯有十三个孩子，甚至还有孙辈。我真不知道他竟然这么——呃——能生。不过，养大十三个孩子，也就难怪他遇到什么都能泰然处之了。

source: I found King Hamlet's abandoned notes describing the end of his life. He was like me. But he gave up, and let madness consume him. He knew and understood everything that was happening around him—his brother's plot against him, his wife turning from him—and he couldn't stop it. Now he remains in Elsinore, neither alive nor fully dead. But why? Will that happen to me, too?
target: 我找到了哈姆雷特国王遗弃的笔记，里面记述了他生命最后阶段的经历。他和我一样。但他放弃了，任由疯狂吞噬了自己。他知道并理解身边发生的一切——弟弟对他的阴谋、妻子对他的疏远——却无法阻止。如今他仍留在埃尔西诺，既非活人，也未彻底死去。但这是为什么？我也会落得同样的下场吗？

source: King Hamlet believes that if he had found a book—the Hand of Dionysus—he could have found a way to put an end to his plight. If this book exists, and is the source of this castle's curse, surely someone has to know something about it.
target: 哈姆雷特国王相信，如果他当初找到一本名为《狄俄尼索斯之手》的书，就能找到摆脱困境的办法。如果这本书存在，而且是城堡诅咒的源头，那一定有人知道些什么。

source: Othello says Simona has been living in Castle Town all along—her identity hidden, I suppose, but it's easier if no one even suspects they ought to be looking for you. She'll return to the bar on Sunday afternoon.
target: 奥赛罗说，西蒙娜一直住在城堡镇——我想，她隐瞒了身份，不过，如果根本没人想到要找你，藏身就容易多了。她会在星期天下午回到酒馆。

source: I... found it. I possess the Book of Fates. So many pieces had to be moved in order for me to find it, but it now sits on my table. The book itself does not provide one exit, but many—and it seems Quince is far from who I thought he was.
target: 我……找到它了。《命运之书》已经在我手里。为了找到它，我不得不改变许多事情，但现在，它就在我的桌上。这本书提供的出路不止一条，而是许多条——看来，奎因斯也远不是我以为的那个人。

source: Apparently Bernardo and Father have been convinced that Fortinbras posed a threat for months, but the King has been reluctant to act. They need more compelling evidence—some source close to Norway that could give me information.
target: 看来，贝尔纳多和父亲几个月来一直认定福丁布拉斯是个威胁，但国王迟迟不愿采取行动。他们需要更有说服力的证据——某个与挪威关系密切的消息来源，或许能向我提供情报。

source: Hamlet is tight-lipped on the spirit—he needs to be sure he can trust me. He's asked me to get information from a diary his mother keeps in her room. Well, if it's what must be done, then so be it.
target: 哈姆雷特对幽灵的事守口如瓶——他需要确定能信任我。他让我从他母亲放在房间里的日记中获取信息。好吧，如果非做不可，那就做吧。

source: King Hamlet's final notes mentioned Quince as 'The Playmaster.' He writes that Quince 'relieved' him of his eternal torment, which explains why he's a spirit in my world and no longer trapped in time. But if Quince has the power to do that, why hasn't he done it for me? What's clear is that all paths seem to lead to me finding this book—this 'Hand of Dionysus.' I'll need to do that before I can understand more.
target: 哈姆雷特国王在最后的笔记中提到奎因斯，称他为“戏剧大师”。他写道，奎因斯让他从永恒的折磨中“解脱”了。这解释了为什么他在我的世界里是个幽灵，不再被困在时间之中。可如果奎因斯有这样的力量，为什么不对我这样做？ 有一点很清楚：所有的路似乎都指向找到那本书——那本《狄俄尼索斯之手》。我得先找到它，才能弄明白更多事情。

source: In various places, I've heard mention of Queen Astrid—Hamlet's grandmother—but I've realized I don't know much about her reign. I could ask around to learn more.
target: 我在不少地方听人提起过阿斯特丽德女王，也就是哈姆雷特的祖母，但我意识到，自己对她在位时的事所知甚少。我可以四处打听，多了解一些。

source: The door to Gertrude's chambers is locked—but I won't let that stop me. There has to be a way to get inside. Someone close to her must know, surely.
target: 乔特鲁德寝室的门锁着，但我不会就此罢休。一定有办法进去。她身边亲近的人肯定知道。

source: Brit agreed to lend me her key—if I set her up for a 'private rendezvous' with Hamlet. Well, if it's what I need to do, the task seems straightforward enough. I'll just try not to think about the consequences.
target: 布莉特答应把钥匙借给我，条件是我替她安排一次与哈姆雷特的“私下幽会”。好吧，如果非做不可，这件事看起来倒不难办。我尽量不去想后果就是了。

source: Irma tells me she would be willing to give me her key to Gertrude's room—if I organize a card game for herself, Lady Brit, Horatio, and Marcellus. I'll have to talk to each person she mentioned individually.
target: 伊尔玛告诉我，她愿意把乔特鲁德房间的钥匙给我，条件是我为她、布莉特女士、霍拉旭和马塞勒斯组织一场牌局。我得分别去找她提到的每个人谈谈。

source: Gertrude's private chambers are always locked when time resets, but now I know how to get inside. The key is hidden in the shrubbery outside the Queen's door—if I retrieve that key, I'll be able to enter freely from now on.
target: 每次时间重置，乔特鲁德寝室的门都会锁上，但现在我知道怎么进去了。钥匙就藏在王后门外的灌木丛里，只要拿到它，以后我就能自由出入。

source: By turning Lady Brit in to Bernardo, I managed to stop her from killing me this loop. It seems my success might be permanent—I was surprised by a visit from Quince, who promised me Brit would never come after my life again. How he intends to accomplish this, I'm unsure, but for now—I wonder what else lies before me.
target: 我向贝尔纳多告发布莉特女士，成功阻止了她在这次循环里杀我。这次成功似乎可能永久有效——奎因斯意外来访，向我保证布莉特再也不会来取我的性命。我不清楚他打算如何做到这一点，但眼下——我想知道，前方还有什么在等着我。

source: Though my father found my warnings disturbing, it doesn't seem telling him alone was enough to save him. Bernardo just informed me of his death—again. I need to know more about how the events played out—and find a way to change the state of that room.
target: 虽然我的警告让父亲感到不安，但看来光是告诉他，还不足以救他。贝尔纳多刚刚又告诉我，父亲死了。我需要进一步了解事情是如何发生的，并想办法改变那个房间里的状况。

source: I... I did it. I actually saved him. Though it did not come without a cost, it meant so much to me to see him live beyond a fate that previously seemed inescapable. I know it's a temporary victory—at the end of these days it will all be reset, and then he will probably die many times, just as before. But now... at least I know something can be done.
target: 我……我做到了。我真的救了他。虽然付出了代价，但看到他逃过那曾经似乎无法避免的命运，继续活下去，对我来说意义重大。我知道这只是暂时的胜利——这几天一结束，一切就会重置，他大概又会像以前那样，一次次死去。但现在……至少我知道，确实有办法改变这一切。

source: Hamlet's madness was brought on not by love, but by a meeting with what he believes to be the spirit of his father. It's from there he must have gotten his information about Claudius's murder. But the information turned out to be correct—so does this spirit actually exist?
target: 哈姆雷特发疯并非因为爱情，而是因为他见到了一个他认为是父亲亡魂的存在。他关于克劳狄斯杀人的消息，想必就是从那里得来的。但消息确实属实——难道这个亡魂真的存在？

source: I've woken up in my bed again, but things feel—different. Strange.
target: 我又在自己的床上醒来，但感觉一切——不一样了。很奇怪。

source: My father was waiting, as usual, but not to chastise me—rather, to invite me to some sort of feast in the Great Hall. I'll need to join everyone there.
target: 父亲像往常一样等着我，但不是为了训斥我——而是邀请我去大厅参加一场宴会。我得去那里和大家会合。

source: I'd forgotten what it was like to see them all happy. This world—this new world—is this the world that would have been without the Book of Fates, without any of it?
target: 我都忘了，看见大家都开开心心是什么感觉。这个世界——这个新的世界——难道就是没有《命运之书》、没有这一切时，本该存在的世界吗？

source: Simona—King Alexander's consort—did not die, but fled the castle. Where could she be?
target: 亚历山大国王的配偶西蒙娜并没有死，而是逃离了城堡。她会在哪里？

source: By night, Bernardo plays a woman onstage—Katherine—in Castle Town.
target: 夜里，贝尔纳多在城堡镇的舞台上扮演一名女性——凯瑟琳。

source: This is all wrong. It's all—
target: 这一切都不对。全都——

source: No—
The death falls hard upon her, my lord.  Perhaps—
target: 他的死对她打击很大，陛下。也许——

source: Your time with Grace—the adventures you embarked on—will vanish.
target: 你与格蕾丝共度的时光——你经历的那些冒险——都将消失。

source: You will never again have the power to overturn nations at your whim. At least—not in the same way.
target: 你将再也没有随心所欲颠覆诸国的力量。至少——无法再以同样的方式做到。
